sections.text: Second, in terms of new product development, old product improvement and innovation, providing new type components and new materials

items: Introduced a series of energy-saving technology products, such as adding gas dynamic system energy-saving technology and products, energy-saving motors, etc.

Each introduction describes many types of new mechanical parts, including some newly developed clutches, couplings, brakes, belt speed reducers, motors, starting and conveying parts, hydraulic components and auxiliary parts, pneumatic components, etc. These products all have advanced technology and energy-saving characteristics.

In terms of new material directions, increased or improved copper and copper alloys, aluminum and aluminum alloys, titanium and titanium alloys, iron and iron alloys and other content. These alloy materials have excellent mechanical properties and physical properties. They can be recycled and reused at high rates. Currently, they are widely used in aviation, aerospace, high-speed rail, computers, communications, electronic products, textiles and printing industries.

sections.text: Third, in terms of promoting standardization work

items: All products, materials and processes adopt new standard materials, such as materials, various mechanical parts, hydraulic and pneumatic components, etc., all have been updated with technical standards and products.

To meet the needs of mechanical product applications, internationalization requirements, following established national standards, and facing international standards on the principle of adopting international standards, such as Chapter 15 'Gear Transmission' has been updated and improved to comply with ISO standards for gear and sprocket design, etc.

The 'Mechanical Design Handbook' Fifth Edition is based on the foundation of the previous Fourth Edition and newly compiled. We borrow from the 'Mechanical Design Handbook' Fifth Edition published version. We sincerely thank all colleagues who provided great support and enthusiastic help for the position and different fields!

Due to the limitations of the author's level, the adjustment work is not comprehensive. Modifications that help avoid omissions and deficiencies are requested. We look forward to readers' continued support and feedback for evaluation.

sections.text: Sixth Edition Preface

The "Handbook of Mechanical Design" has been published since 1969 in its first edition and has been revised five times. Sales have exceeded 1.3 million copies, becoming a new Chinese classic. As a national key scientific and technological reference book, the "Handbook of Mechanical Design" has won numerous national and provincial awards. Among them, it won the National Science and Technology Achievement Award in 1978, the Ministry of Labor Science and Technology Award in 1983, the National Excellent Science and Technology Book Second Prize in 1995, the National Chemical Industry Technology Progress Second Prize in 1999, the National Petroleum and Chemical Industry Science and Technology Progress Second Prize in 2002, and the National Petroleum and Chemical Industry Science and Technology Progress Second Prize in 2003. From 1986 to 2015, it was repeatedly rated as a national excellent sales book.

In keeping with the times, opening up and innovating, achieving practicality, and pursuing the best combination of rigor and creativity, promoting the broad mechanical design personnel to develop better and newer products, adapting to market and production needs, improving market competitiveness and international competitiveness, this is the "Handbook of Mechanical Design" has always adhered to and unremitting pursuit of the highest goal.

The "Handbook of Mechanical Design" (hereinafter referred to as the "Handbook") fifth edition has been published for 8 years. During this period, we conducted extensive research and investigation, invited many experts in the mechanical field, held academic seminars, and listened to suggestions from colleagues in the sixth edition revision. We went deep into design institutes, factories and mines on the front line to understand the application of the "Handbook" and the wishes of designers, and discovered that in the production practice of enterprises, there are new experimental and new problems, multiple channels and multiple sources of information, collecting new technologies and new products both domestically and internationally, improving and enriching the content of the "Handbook", making the "Handbook" more vibrant, maximizing the improvement of the broad mechanical design personnel's main innovation ability, and adapting to the needs of building an innovative national economy.
The specific revision details of the sixth edition of the "Handbook" are as follows.
1. Improving product development and innovative design

items: Added Chapter 5 "Mechanical Product Structure Design", which provides 12 commonly used mechanical product structure design rules for product designers to refer to.
Chapter 1 "General Design Materials" added new examples and typical examples of mechanical product design.
Chapter 11 "Lubrication and Sealing" added design calculation content for common lubrication device design, adapting to the design needs of new lubricating products and development.

Chapter 15 "Gear Drive" further improved the design of involute gears in accordance with ISO international standards, non-variable tooth profile design, point contact design, multi-point contact flexible drive design, etc. For example, added calculation examples of involute gears conforming to ISO standards, improving gear accuracy.
Chapter 23 "Pneumatic Drive" added content on pneumatic module electro-pneumatic combined drive technology, pneumatic system energy efficiency, etc.

sections.text: 《Mechanical Design Manual》Sixth Edition Volume 5 covers all content of mechanical design specifications. Volume 1 includes design data, mechanical transmission, gears and combinations, shape and position tolerances and surface structure, common mechanical engineering materials, machinery, machine product structure design; Volume 2 covers shaft connections and seals, shaft sealing, shaft, lifting and running machinery parts, operations, small five-axis components; Volume 3 covers lubrication, sealing, springs, screws, common motors, electrical equipment and motors (liquid) rod and piston, mechanical transmission control and application, mechanical design; Volume 5 covers hydraulic transmission, hydraulic control, gas transmission, etc.

《Mechanical Design Manual》Sixth Edition is based on the composition of the previous edition, expanding the scope of application and learning of 《Mechanical Design Manual》. It maintains the style and characteristics of the previous edition, emphasizing practicality, from the perspective of mechanical design personnel, combining reasonable arrangement of content, emphasis on fundamentals, data, and information. It selects examples from long-term engineering practice, reflects advanced nature, increases the application scope of previous materials, new methods, new technologies, new processes, adopts new standards and specifications, widely collects materials with advanced years and implements standardization of new products. It highlights practicality, facilitates use, and characteristics. 《Mechanical Design Manual》can serve as a tool book for mechanical designers and related engineering technicians, and can also be used as a reference book for colleges and universities for specialist teachers to use.

3.2 Application Examples of Preference Numbers

When designing products, the basic parameter series of products should preferentially use preference number series. For standard parts, product families with many varieties, should investigate and analyze the addition of preference numbers, and use the preference number series suitable for the product as the main parameter series. In the system design of learning parts, the preference number should be selected—some important dimensions should be used as preference numbers. The following is a starting machine roller structure dimension design example. The main roller structure dimension diagram is shown in Figure 1-1-1.

(1) Determine the preference number of the roller diameter
For roller diameter, the most important parameter is the wire rope diameter d. Since d is small, the wire rope diameter has a small influence on the roller diameter, thus determining the roller structural dimensions. Therefore, first use the wire rope diameter d as the preference number, take R20 series, dimensions in the range of 10-60mm. Next, in the roller structure part, several wire rope diameters, determine the wire rope center distance D and use preference numbers, and the roller bottom diameter D_b is calculated as follows:
D_b = D - d_t

In addition, according to experimental verification of the shape, its dimensions are as shown in Figure 1-1-1, the ratio coefficient is preference number. This only requires the bottom radius r to take preference numbers, the side shape of each part dimension is also preference number.
The outer diameter D_a of the roller is calculated as follows:
D_a = D_b + 2H

D_a—generally not a preference number.
The axial combined dimension—a certain axial length l and roller hole diameter d are preference numbers.

(2) Determine the roller diameter D
The roller diameter D series by R20 series, the roller diameter and wire rope diameter ratio determines the starting machine structural specification. In the starting machine structure specification, the maximum is 20 times. The series design assumes 20 times, 25 times and 31.5 times three types (preference numbers are also selected, ensuring D is preference number), and 20 times roller diameter is 20 type, 25 times is 25 type, 31.5 times is 31.5 type. For different wire rope diameters d, the roller diameter D can be selected according to the R20 series table (see Table 1-1-39).

3 Preferred Numbers and Preferred Number Series

Preferred numbers and preferred number series are a type of scientific and standardized number system. The main parameters of products or parts are arranged according to preferred number series, which can make products or parts systematic, standardized, and use preferred numbers for series design, which is convenient for analyzing the relationships between parameters, reducing design calculation work, and their parameter series can be compared and managed economically, which can meet the requirements of coordinating various departments and professional intervals.
3.1 Preferred Number Series (Extracted from GB/T 321—2005, GB/T 19763—2005)

Preferred numbers are defined as ¹⁰√10, ¹⁰√10, ²⁰√10, ⁴⁰√10 and ⁸⁰√10, and the values contain 10 preferred numbers at various levels of the common logarithm. Each series is represented by R5, R10, R20, R40 and R80, respectively, divided into R5 series, R10 series, R20 series, R40 series and R80 series. The series are classified into basic series, supplementary series, derivative series (including derived series and composite series) and modified series. Table 1-1-38 lists the values of 1-10 of the 10 series. For values greater than 10 and less than 1, they can be obtained by the method of extending forward.

(5) Calculate the axial load P that the shaft bearing receives
The axial load P received by the shaft bearing is equal to the tension of the steel wire rope P₀, that is:
P = 2P₀ = 2x(P₀/n - P₀/3)

Where: P₀ — steel wire rope tension; P₀ — steel wire rope breaking load, which can be obtained from the standard diameter of the steel wire rope; n — safety factor, for heavy machinery steel wire rope n = 6.

When the steel wire rope diameter d₁ = 10mm, the table P₀ = 60.3kN, then P = 20.1kN, approximately as the priority number P = 20kN. At the same time, consider the material of the shaft to ensure that the bearing load P₀ of the steel wire rope does not change, the steel wire rope diameter d₁ is R20 series, the load P is R20/2 series (because P = 20kN is R10 series in the middle, so R20/2 = R10 series).
(6) Determine the hole diameter d and groove depth l

Set the hole diameter d according to R20 series, the groove depth l according to R10 series. For the same steel wire rope diameter d₁ pulley, the bearing load P is different, so there must be different holes d and groove depths l. Because the groove width A is fixed at a large limit, this is the best use of the priority number system for analysis.
1) Determine the hole diameter d and pulley length l relationship
The relationship between the hole diameter d and the pulley length l can be determined by the allowable pressure on the shaft surface, which is as follows:
l = (P × d₁²)/(dB₀ × d)
Where: B₀ — shaft bearing pressure, set B₀ = 900N/cm²; P — pulley bearing load, N₁; l, d unit cm.
For each steel wire rope diameter d₁, its B₀ and P are constant, so the above formula can be expressed as:
l ∝ 1/d

sections.text: 2. Series selection principle

items: When selecting parameter series, the preferred number with the least (relative difference maximum) basic series should be used, that is, R5 series first, then R10 series, then R20 series, then R40 series. (Relative difference = (rear-front)/front × 100%, each series ratio: R5=60%; R10=25%; R20=12%; R40=6%; R80=3%) Supplement series R80 can be used less, only in the case of special refinement of the basic series in the preferred number can not be used standard situation.

The basic series of the same level can not be mixed, otherwise, sparse series should be selected. Select sparse series, should follow the preferred number R5/2, R10/3, R10/5, R20/3, R20/4, R40/3, R40/5.

In the case of insufficient space for the series, it is not allowed to use preferred numbers, and it is allowed to use standard specifications (see Table 6 with '-' number). If the sparse series is the preferred number of the common value, part of the sparse series is the series, the parameter value is not within the sparse series range, it is not allowed to use. Partial Fraction Decomposition

The fifth and higher order algebraic equations have a general algebraic solution method (the system of equations formed by the coefficients is limited to four operations and square root operations). This is the partial fraction decomposition.
Fractional Operations
a/b + c/b = (a+c)/b; a/b + c/d = (ad+bc)/bd
a/b × c/d = ac/bd; a/b ÷ c/d = ad/bc
(a/b)^n = a^n/b^n; ⁿ√(a/b) = ⁿ√a/ⁿ√b (a>0, b>0)
Partial Fraction Decomposition

If a proper fraction (the degree of the numerator is less than the degree of the denominator) can be decomposed into the form (x-a)^r or (x²+px+q)^s (where p²/4 - q < 0) as the basic partial fraction form, and its expansion is called partial fraction decomposition. If the proper fraction (the degree of the numerator is not less than the degree of the denominator), it should first be converted to the form of a proper fraction plus a polynomial, then partial fraction decomposition is performed. The various systems of partial fraction decomposition can be determined by the following fixed coefficient method. Below are several cases described.

Properties of Row and Column Determinants
Row, column exchange for determinant, its value does not change:

|a₁ b₁ c₁| = |a₁ a₂ a₃|
|a₂ b₂ c₂|   |b₁ b₂ b₃|
|a₃ b₃ c₃|   |c₁ c₂ c₃|
If two rows (or two columns) have proportional corresponding elements, the value is zero:

|a₁ b₁ c₁| = |ka₁ b₁ c₁|
|a₂ b₂ c₂|   |ka₂ b₂ c₂| = 0
|a₃ b₃ c₃|   |ka₃ b₃ c₃|
Two rows (or two columns) are swapped, the determinant changes sign:

|a₁ b₁ c₁| = -|a₃ b₃ c₃|
|a₂ b₂ c₂|    |a₂ b₂ c₂|
|a₃ b₃ c₃|    |a₁ b₁ c₁|
If a row (or column) is multiplied by a non-zero constant k, the determinant value is multiplied by k:

|a₁ kb₁ c₁| = k|a₁ b₁ c₁|
|a₂ kb₂ c₂|    |a₂ b₂ c₂|
|a₃ kb₃ c₃|    |a₃ b₃ c₃|
The properties of row and column determinants can be extended to higher-order determinants
If a row (or column) of an element is the sum of two elements, the determinant can be decomposed into the sum of two determinants of the same form:

|a₁+d b₁+e c₁+f| = |a₁ b₁ c₁| + |d e f|
|a₂   b₂   c₂  |   |a₂ b₂ c₂|   |a₂ b₂ c₂|
|a₃   b₃   c₃  |   |a₃ b₃ c₃|   |a₃ b₃ c₃|
If a row (or column) of all elements are the same number, adding the same multiple of another row (or column) to it, the determinant value does not change:

|a₁ b₁+kc₁ c₁| = |a₁ b₁ c₁|
|a₂ b₂+kc₂ c₂|   |a₂ b₂ c₂|
|a₃ b₃+kc₃ c₃|   |a₃ b₃ c₃|
Algebraic Cofactor and Its Application in Determinant Expansion
The element aᵢⱼ in the i-th row and j-th column of a determinant, deleting the i-th row and j-th column, the remaining low-order determinant is called the minor Mᵢⱼ of the element aᵢⱼ.

(1) Solution of higher-order linear differential equations with constant coefficients

Using D to represent d/dx, D² to represent d²/dx², ..., the higher-order linear differential equation becomes: (Dⁿ+p₁Dⁿ⁻¹+p₂Dⁿ⁻²+...+pₙ₋₁D+pₙ)y=0, which can be written as containing D's n-degree polynomial equation (Dⁿ+p₁Dⁿ⁻¹+p₂Dⁿ⁻²+...+pₙ₋₁D+pₙ)y=0. That is, L(D)=Dⁿ+p₁Dⁿ⁻¹+p₂Dⁿ⁻²+...+pₙ₋₁D+pₙ. The equation L(D)y=0. According to the factorization rule (D-r₁)···(D-rₙ)y=0, that is (D-r₁)y=0,...,(D-rₙ)y=0, r₁,...,rₙ, then these linear differential equations (called characteristic equations) have: dy/dx=r₁y; dy/dx=r₁y; dy/dx=∫r₁dx; lny=r₁x+C₁; y=e^(r₁x)=C₁e^(r₁x). By this reasoning, (D-rₖ)y=0, dy/dx=rₖy; dy/dx=rₖdx; dy/dx=∫rₖdx; lny=rₖx+C₂; y=e^(rₖx+C₂)=Cₖe^(rₖx), so y=C₁e^(r₁x)+C₂e^(r₂x)+...+Cₙe^(rₙx). This table shows that the solution of the higher-order linear differential equation is e^(e)'s form.
(2) Solution of first-order linear non-homogeneous differential equations

Its characteristic root is a first-order use of the exponential substitution method, but it is better to use the integrating factor method to simplify, clear, pass, special, first-order linear non-homogeneous method.
Set dy/dx+p(x)y=f(x), multiply both sides by the integrating factor e^(∫p(x)dx):
dy/dx·e^(∫p(x)dx) + p(x)y·e^(∫p(x)dx) = f(x)e^(∫p(x)dx)
d[ye^(∫p(x)dx)]/dx = f(x)e^(∫p(x)dx)
ye^(∫p(x)dx) = ∫f(x)e^(∫p(x)dx)dx + C
y = e^(-∫p(x)dx)[∫f(x)e^(∫p(x)dx)dx + C]
Laplace Transform

The definition of Laplace transform: set two functions f(t) when t≥0 have meaning, and f(t) is a piecewise continuous function or piecewise smooth function; f(t) is of exponential order, that is, when t is sufficiently large, there exists |f(t)|≤Meᶜᵗ, where M, C are real numbers, then
L[f(t)] = ∫₀^∞ f(t)e^(-st)dt = F(s)

Called the Laplace transform of the function f(t), abbreviated as Laplace transform, and use the symbol 'L' to denote, where f(t) is called the original function, the image function F(s) obtained is called the image function, and s is called the Laplace operator.
If L[f(t)]=F(s), then
L⁻¹[F(s)]=f(t)
Called the inverse Laplace transform.

1) For the two-sided Laplace transform of the opposite function (combined with the initial condition), let L{x(t)} = X(s), that is, X(s) is the first-order algebraic equation of x(t), then solve for X(s).

2) For the Laplace transform of x(s) to perform two-sided Laplace inverse transform (can be obtained through partial fraction decomposition), if the expression x(s) = A(s)/B(s) has the right side as a rational function, then it can be decomposed into partial fractions and the Laplace inverse transform table can be used to find the solution, with the simplest form of the parameters as the solution that satisfies the initial conditions.

sections.text: Finite element method is based on the principle of dividing the domain into subdomains. Absorbing the idea of variation of the problem, it develops a kind of approximate value method. It puts the limit of freedom of choice of the approximate function within a certain degree of freedom (Ω is the number of nodes in the domain). The problem of determining the approximate function is transformed into a problem of determining the values of the nodes and their fixed number of node values in the domain Ω, called the unit element.
The expression is as follows:
∫_Ω f(x,y,y') dx
δ∫_Ω f(x,y,y') dx is called the variation of the integrand; δ∫_Ω f(x,y,y')dx = 0 is the condition for the extremum of the integrand.
(1) Several Concepts

① Extremal curve (function). Through the given point A, B of the curve (function) y = y(x), the function y(x) and y'(x) are continuous on the interval [a₀, a₁], find the sample function, so that the integrand
J(y) = ∫_{a₀}^{a₁} F(x,y,y') dx
obtains the maximum or minimum value. The curve (function) y = y₀(x) of the extremum is called the extremal curve (function) y = y₀(x).

② Admissible curve. Satisfying the conditions y(a₀) = b₀, y(a₁) = b₁ and the smooth curve y = y(x) is called the admissible curve. Through the points M₀(a₀,b₀), M₁(a₁,b₁) the curve is called the permissible curve.
y(x,α) = y₀(x) + α[y(α) - y₀(x)]

In the formula, α is an arbitrary number, ensuring that the curve y(x,α) in the variation δy = y(x) - y₀(x), y(x,α) = y₀(x) + αδy can guide the curve on the line y(x, α) = y₀(x) to reach the extremum, then y = y₀(x)

If F does not contain x, this integrand

is the Euler equation that can be reduced to a first-order equation F - y'F'_{y'} = C.

sections.text: The stress state at any point in a loaded body can be completely described by the normal stress and shear stress on a plane passing through that point. The stress circle (Mohr's circle) is a graphical method for determining the stress components on any inclined plane. The principal stresses are the maximum and minimum normal stresses, and they occur on planes where the shear stress is zero. The maximum shear stress is equal to half the difference between the principal stresses.

sections.text: Allowable Stress and Safety Factor

For standard parts used in special machinery, their allowable stress and safety factor are usually determined by the design of the machine. However, for standard parts or parts with special shapes or dimensions that are not restricted by the machine, the allowable stress σₑ and safety factor S must be selected by the designer. The relationship between working stress σ and allowable stress σₑ is:
σₑ ≤ σₚ

Formula: Kₛ is the safety factor; σlim is the material strength limit. The symbols or definitions of σ or σₑ are also based on the relative meaning of τ.
For plastic materials: σlim = σₛ (yield strength calculation)
For brittle materials: σlim = σb
Since σ is related to the actual stress in the calculation, the named stress σₑ corresponding to the actual working stress F on the working stress, therefore, there is also:
Kₛ = F₀/F

The safety factor Kₛ and the type of load on the machine are closely related. When static load is applied, the danger of overload is small, and the safety factor should be used as the maximum load (named load increase static load). When static load passes through the danger, use the maximum load that is not beneficial to the condition to calculate the maximum total force as Fₑ. This ensures that the force occurs at one time.

The precise value of Kₛ can only be obtained through comparison of similar structures or similar machinery. If there is no precise and accurate Kₛ value, you can refer to Table 1-1-87 for recommended values, or you can refer to Table 1-1-88 for values.

5.3 Contact Stress

In high-speed machinery, the theory states that contact stress is transmitted through point or line contact. In practice, under load, the contact surface undergoes elastic deformation. Due to the small contact area, this creates very high local stress at the contact point. The contact stress is the reaction force of the elastic deformation of the contact surface. The machine element experiences contact stress as a change in force, and the loss of contact is the elastic recovery of the contact surface. The stress is expressed as the pressure on the contact surface, which gradually increases, causing metal fatigue and wear. The influence of contact stress on the fatigue life of the contact surface is significant. The contact area and the distribution of contact stress depend on the shape and size of the contact surface. Therefore, the contact stress on the contact surface is the maximum contact stress. According to the theory of contact stress, the dangerous point of calculation is σ_rn = 0.6σ_max. For the contact problem with strong stress concentration, the dangerous point condition is σ_max ≤ σ_rp.
Where σ_HP—contact stress, related to material properties and heat treatment conditions, point line contact, dynamic or static contact, see Table 1-1-107 to Table 1-1-109.

When the impact time is short (the time for the load to act on the structure is much less than half the natural vibration period), the impact load on the structure is called impact load. Its effect on the deformation and stress calculation is equivalent to multiplying the static load by a dynamic system number. Impact load calculation formula is as follows:
(1) When the mass of the impacting object is much larger than the mass of the impacted object (5-10 times or more), the mass of the impacting object can be ignored.
(2) When the shape of the impacted object changes significantly and is not rigid, the impacted object is treated as elastic.

rows: Single Crystal High Temperature Alloy Casting

Due to the development of directional solidification and withdrawal casting technology, it has developed into a directional solidification technology that can directly produce castings with single crystal structure at high temperatures. This precision casting technology is in the blank space of aviation and aerospace applications. From the 20th to 60 years of the 20th century, directional solidification composite castings have developed 20 types of single crystal alloys. rows: Utilizes the principle that by controlling the cooling rate and solidification direction of semi-solid metal materials, or by adding certain semi-solid composite materials to achieve semi-solid shape, or by converting such materials into semi-solid composite shape. This method is called semi-solid metal casting, which is divided into two categories according to the process method.

Due to the semi-solid metal composite being at high temperature, heat transfer is convenient, and it is easy to achieve automated control. For this reason, semi-solid metal casting has become an important process method. However, the process is short, the structure is more uniform, and the semi-solid metal composite casting defects are significantly reduced. In practice, the application example is: using semi-solid casting method in 1997, the United States successfully developed semi-solid composite casting technology for automobile engine cylinder blocks with a total weight of 240 million units, oil pan and engine support frame of 100 million units, steering gear 150-200 million units, and belt pulley 20 million units. Another company uses semi-solid composite casting technology to produce 50 million units of automobile engine composite castings. Beijing University of Science and Technology successfully developed semi-solid casting of AISi7Mg composite materials, and developed engine block castings and other parts, and conducted experimental verification.

Is a method that uses a closed mold cavity to control the cooling and solidification direction of semi-solid metal materials, and directly sends it to the forming machine, casting and cooling to form. Using the casting machine's behavior as the change in casting, using the most machine-like shape, called flow casting.

Also uses a closed mold cavity and other methods to extract the shape of semi-solid metal materials, and further solidifies and cools the material. After the squeeze casting is divided into a small size, and the new hot semi-solid metal cavity is filled, using the machine to transport the semi-solid shape into the mold, performing casting and cooling. According to the application of the machine, also called as squeeze casting, squeeze cooling, etc.

rows: (1) Selective laser sintering combined with selective characteristic solidification (SLS)

This type of technology uses a laser beam to scan and sinter powder materials layer by layer according to the cross-sectional shape information provided by the computer. The laser beam has a power of 10-200mW, with a wavelength of 320-370nm. The scanning system is controlled by a computer. The powder material is heated to near its melting point, and the laser beam scans the powder surface in the X-Y direction to perform sintering operations. After sintering one layer, the work platform descends by one layer thickness, and a new layer of powder is spread on top. The process is repeated until the entire part is completed. The shape of the part is determined by the contour line on the work platform surface. The sintered part has high density, good mechanical properties, and can be directly used without post-processing.

This type of technology uses a laser to cut and separate material sheets layer by layer according to the cross-sectional shape information provided by the computer. The material sheets are stacked and bonded together using adhesive. The laser cuts along the contour line of each layer, and the waste material is removed. The process is repeated until the entire part is completed. The shape of the part is determined by the contour line on each layer. The laminated part has good dimensional accuracy and surface quality.
Suitable for complex shapes, large-scale and multi-mold products

(3) Fused deposition modeling (FDM) - This is a molding method whose principle is shown in Figure 11. The heating head moves in the calculated X-Y plane and Z-axis direction. After the fused deposition material, such as ABS and MABS plastic, nylon, polyester resin, etc., is heated and melted, it is sprayed onto the nozzle. After the nozzle is heated to the melting point, it is sprayed onto the substrate and cooled to form a layer. The next layer is sprayed on top of the previous layer. After multiple layers are stacked, the final three-dimensional product is formed. Due to the low molding speed, it can be used for thermal spraying treatment. Since the nozzle diameter is small, the heating power is not large, so it is mainly used for small-sized fused deposition materials.
Applicable to small parts and nozzles in composite molding

(4) Thermoplastic material selective sintering (TDP) - This is a multi-nozzle spray head controlled by a computer. According to the information recorded on the sintering information carrier, a layer of thermoplastic material is selectively sprayed on the substrate to form a sintered layer. After the first layer is completely sintered, the work table drops down one layer height, and the next layer is sintered. If this process is repeated, the final three-dimensional product is formed. The work table must be kept in the heating furnace to further solidify the sintered layer to ensure sintering strength. Its working principle is shown in Figure 12.

sections.text: Chapter 3 Forging, Stamping and Deep Drawing Design Process and Structural Elements
1 Forging
1.1 Forgeability of Metal Materials

The forgeability of metal materials refers to the ability of metal materials to undergo plastic deformation without cracking during the forging process. Generally, low-carbon steels with carbon content below certain limits have good forgeability. Among them, low-carbon steel has the best forgeability, with uniform structure and low segregation. Low-alloy steel has good forgeability, with uniform structure and low segregation. When carbon content reaches 2.2%, it is difficult to forge. Low-alloy steel has the best forgeability, similar to medium-carbon steel. High-alloy steel forging is difficult. For carbon steel, its forgeability is poor; if it has special points: (1) low thermal conductivity, high deformation resistance, especially for alloys containing high thermal conductivity and high strength; (2) high deformation temperature range, generally the forging temperature range is 350-400°C, while alloy steel has only 100-200°C; (3) variable deformation resistance, hardening effect is significant, high-alloy steel forging temperature is lower than the deformation temperature, which can avoid excessive deformation and cracking; (4) low plasticity, some overheated steel forging deformation is 60%, and has high-alloy steel only 5%-8 times.

Aluminum alloys: Low-carbon alloys can produce various shapes of forgings, can be self-lubricated, molded, pressed, rolled and drilled, but generally, aluminum alloys require 30% of the low-carbon content, its forging plasticity is low, and the model forging flow plasticity ratio is large, the highest temperature range is within 150°C, and even some high-strength aluminum alloys are below 100°C.

Forged aluminum alloys have the following types: (1) Al-Mg-Si series alloys, such as LD2 with good plasticity and corrosion resistance, easy to forge, but low strength; (2) Al-Mg-Si-Cu alloys, such as LD5, LD6, LD9, LD10, with higher strength, can be forged, two types are distinguished by subsequent addition of copper and titanium, LD10 due to having higher strength, so strength is higher, hot forging is not suitable for LD5, so use high-strength forming forgings, due to its material properties and corrosion resistance, so it is not suitable for thin-walled parts; (3) Al-Cu-Mg-Fe-Ni alloys, such as LD7, LD8, these alloys have high iron content, so have high heat resistance, called heat-resistant aluminum, use T-type solution treatment, quenching, guide ring and other high-temperature parts. LD7 compared to LD8 has higher strength and plasticity, especially high-temperature plasticity is good.

Copper alloys have good forgeability in general. The most important is brass (60Cu-38Zn-2Pb), brass (60Cu-39-25Zn-0.75Sn, also called sea brass) and brass (58.5Cu-39Zn-1.4Fe-1Sn-0.1Mn) have better plasticity. Compared with steel alloys, copper alloys have lower initial forging temperature, highest temperature range is 100-200°C, at 250-650°C has good plasticity range, but requires higher forging ability than carbon steel, copper brass 20-200°C low temperature 650-900°C high temperature, are very poor plasticity, that is, hot state and cold state cannot be forged, some special brass (such as brass with lead) plastic is low, difficult to forge. Brass with Sn<10% tin brass, brass with P 0.1%-0.4%, brass with Sn<7% tin brass can be forged, brass with Al>9% when forged, if the brass cannot be forged, brass with Sn>10% tin brass cannot be forged. Brass forging is limited, just heat forging and cold forging are relatively difficult.

Titanium alloys are not rust-resistant, poor forgeability. It is at the highest temperature without deformation resistance of steel is very large, and the temperature of the lower surface is rigid and high, compared to steel also has more, change the speed is sensitive to the combined deformation resistance of the deformation resistance is small, flow is poor, model forging viscosity shows that its metal sound is heavy, and because titanium alloys after heat treatment will produce stress corrosion cracking, for specific corrosion resistance, also increases the difficulty of titanium alloy forging.

(3) Design principles for multiple pulling depths
For grooved circular groove-shaped parts, multiple pulling depths should be designed according to the following principles:

items: For parts with groove diameter ratio (dL/d = 1.1-1.4), several pulling depths should not exceed the groove or only slightly exceed the groove and corner parts. In the subsequent pulling depth, the groove shape should be maintained and the bottom of the groove should be kept flat.

For parts with groove diameter ratio (dL/d > 1.4), the first pulling depth should form the groove shape required by the drawing. At the same time, the pulling depth should be kept at the groove diameter, and the subsequent pulling depth should maintain the groove shape.

a. When the groove diameter ratio is too large, the first pulling depth should reach the groove and corner parts that are half the groove diameter smaller than the corner radius. In the subsequent pulling depth, the groove height should be kept basically unchanged, with only a small groove diameter and corner radius change.
b. When the groove diameter ratio is small and the first pulling depth groove diameter is half the groove diameter smaller than the corner radius, the first pulling depth should be designed according to the normal groove diameter ratio, and in the subsequent pulling depth, the groove diameter should be kept basically unchanged, with only a small groove diameter increase.

To prevent the groove diameter from being too large in the subsequent pulling depth, the groove diameter should be increased by 3%-10%. For materials with large elongation, the groove diameter should be placed in the subsequent pulling depth. This will shift the 1.5%-3% groove diameter distribution to the groove position, making the groove diameter increase.

When the groove diameter and corner radius are too small, the groove diameter can be appropriately increased by half the groove diameter, and then the groove shape should be reshaped. The corner radius dimension should meet the requirements.

1.2 Weldability of Metals

The weldability of metals depends on the welding method, process parameters, and other factors. For the same metal, different welding methods or process parameters may result in significant differences in weldability. When designing, attention must be paid to the weld structure, rigidity, welding method, welding materials, and welding process conditions, considering the weldability of the material. For important welded structures, weldability tests must be conducted and suitable welding materials selected.
Weldability of Steel

The weldability of steel can be evaluated through appropriate public formulas or weldability tests on steel. The carbon equivalent is the basic basis for evaluating the effect of chemical composition on material weld joint performance, and is a method to evaluate the tendency of cold cracks in welds and the hardness trend of the heat-affected zone.
The carbon equivalent and low-alloy steel formulas commonly used in carbon steel and low-alloy steel are (recommended by the International Welding Society) as follows:
CE = C + Mn/6 + (Cr+Mo+V)/5 + (Ni+Cu)/15
For alloy steel with C ≤ 0.5%, Mn ≤ 1.6%, Cr ≤ 1%, Ni ≤ 3.5%, Mo ≤ 0.6%, Cu ≤ 1% alloy steel, the carbon equivalent formula is recommended as follows:
CE = C + Mn/6 + Cr+V/5 + Ni/15 + Mo+Si/4 + Cu/13 + P/2

(3) Mixed gas: The mechanical and chemical properties of the shielding gas in the welding process, from the initial isolation of the air, protect the weld area from oxidation. This is the main function of the mixed gas, such as powder, flux, large stone, limestone, etc.

(5) Alloying: Its main function is to form alloy elements in the weld, which can improve the mechanical properties of the weld. Alloy elements commonly used include manganese, chromium, nickel, etc.
(6) Deoxidation: To prevent the weld material from being oxidized to the limit, and prevent the weld from having a certain degree, to prevent the weld from having strong brittleness, commonly used deoxidizers include silicon powder, aluminum powder, etc.
(7) Desulfurization: Add some desulfurizing agents to the weld to have a certain degree of desulfurization, ductility and fluidity, to prevent the weld from being brittle, to prevent the weld surface from being smooth and not rough. The welding wire is composed of a certain amount of deoxidizers in the wire, such as Si, Mn, Ti, etc. If the alloy content is insufficient, the deoxidizer in the wire will produce pores, and the welding chemical properties (especially alkalinity) will decrease.

Using the alloy elements contained in the wire to perform deoxidation and deoxidation during the welding process, to prevent nitrogen from entering the welding torch, to prevent nitrogen from entering the welding torch, to prevent nitrogen from entering the welding torch, and to add a strong deoxidizer such as C, Si, Mn, and other elements such as Ti, Zr, Al, Ce, etc.

Flux-cored wire is a tubular wire with a flux core inside, composed of a steel sheath filled with flux powder. It is also called flux-cored wire, cored wire, or flux-cored wire. It uses gas or liquid protection, and the flux inside protects the molten pool during welding, making it easy to implement high-quality welding. According to the development direction of welding materials, it can be divided into two types: flux-cored wire and non-flux-cored wire.

sections.caption: Classification and Application of Flux-Cored Wire
rows: Gas-shielded flux-cored wire (with external gas protection)

The surface morphology of flux-cored wire is divided into simple cross-section and complex cross-section. The folding shape is different, and the shape is T-shaped, E-shaped, and middle-shaped, etc.

Quality Requirements Based on Welding Components

The main advantage is that it can ensure good corrosion resistance and good toughness at low temperatures. The main disadvantage is that it requires large heat input during welding, which may cause sensitization of the austenitic stainless steel. The austenitic stainless steel has poor thermal conductivity and large linear expansion coefficient. During welding, it is easy to cause hot cracking and residual stress. To prevent cracking, preheating and slow cooling should be used. The material is prone to austenitic grain growth during high-temperature heating. Under no preheating conditions, to prevent cracking, use low-hydrogen welding materials. (8) Efficiency relationship: η = (Useful power output)/(Input power) × 100%.

Filler metal to filler metal matching

Different welding methods have different requirements for filler metal performance. When selecting filler metal for multi-layer welding, the composition of the deposited metal should be based on the final layer requirements. The alloy elements in the filler metal should be selected to avoid excessive dilution of the base metal, which may cause brittleness, cracking, and segregation.

Different products have different requirements for welding structure and performance. It is possible to use lower alloy content or use multiple methods such as heat treatment, stress relief, and process control to meet the requirements. However, for a specific welding structure, the selection of filler metal is the most important.

The welding structure design should consider the complexity of the welding method, the shape of the filler metal, the size of the weld, and whether the shape can be achieved. This should be considered when selecting the filler metal to ensure the feasibility of the welding process.

sections.text: 1.6 Brazing

Brazing is a method that uses filler metal with a lower melting point than the base metal, heating the workpiece and filler metal to above the brazing point, below the melting point of the base metal, and using liquid filler metal and wetting material to fill the gap between the base metal and achieve a solid connection of the workpiece.

During brazing, the heating temperature is low, the thermal stress and strain of the joint are small, the deformation is small, the joint is smooth, the process is simple, and the production efficiency is high. Therefore, brazing is widely used.

The brazing point is generally lower than the melting point of the base metal, so it must use brazing to achieve the strength of the base metal. The brazing joint is connected in a short time, and the residual brazing joint has good corrosion resistance. Therefore, the assembly and cleaning of the brazing joint after brazing must be strictly controlled.

According to the material's brazing temperature and brazing joint strength, brazing materials are divided into: hard brazing (brazing material, brazing temperature above 450°C), easy brazing (brazing material, brazing temperature below 450°C). See Table 1-4-73 and Table 1-4-74 for brazing materials. To achieve high-quality brazing joints, the appropriate brazing method should be selected according to the brazing material, joint structure and size, joint usage performance, production efficiency and equipment conditions, and correctly select the corresponding brazing method, material, and brazing process.

sections.text: 2 Riveted Joints
2.1 Design Considerations for Riveted Joints

items: The line force in the center of the rivet should coincide with the line of action of the force.
The rivet diameter should not exceed 5d. Use a rivet head with a hemispherical shape. The total thickness should be 7 times the rivet diameter.
For single-row riveted joints, the rivet spacing should not be too small. Generally, both sides should be used.
The pitch of riveted joints should be at least 20% larger than the hole diameter. Therefore, the hole spacing method cannot be used for structural members.
Cold rivets should generally use straight holes smaller than 8 mm. Acceptance is not required. Do not use heavy rivets in this location.
Plates larger than 4 mm must be able to perform beveling. Plates smaller than 4 mm require very tight riveting. You can apply aluminum powder to the copper plate gap to obtain a tight seal.
Industrial rivets should be made of rivets. They should use force to reduce the force.
Avoid using welded rivets as much as possible.
Ensure that the number of rivets on the same surface is minimized. Arrange rivets in a staggered pattern (see Table 1-4-84 item a).
For multi-layer riveted joints, the layer spacing of the rivet holes should be consistent (see Table 1-4-84 item b).
In transmission riveted joints, the rivets in the direction of force transmission should not exceed 6, but should be at least 2 (see Table 1-4-84 item c).

sections.text: Chapter 5 Design Process and Structural Elements of Cold Processing of Zero Parts
1 Machinability of Metal Materials

The machinability of metal materials refers to the difficulty of cutting and processing a workpiece to meet the required precision. The factors affecting machinability are numerous. To date, there is no single method that can comprehensively reflect the machinability of materials. Generally, based on specific conditions, different methods are used to express it. The cutting speed V60 commonly used in production is the cutting speed when the tool life is 60 minutes. V60 is high, indicating good machinability of the material. If σn = 600MPa for 45 steel, V60 is used as the base, denoted as (V60)1. If the V60 of other materials is (V60)i, compared with it, the relative machinability index Kn = (V60)i/(V60)1 is called the relative machinability index. The relative machinability index of commonly used materials is shown in Table 1-5-1.

sections.caption: Table 1-5-1 Relative Machinability of Commonly Used Materials (Reference)

sections.text: Based on the analysis of the physical properties of metals, generally when the hardness is 170-230HB, the machinability is good. When the hardness exceeds 230HB, it is difficult to machine. When HB>300, the machinability is significantly reduced; when HB=400, the machinability is very poor. When the hardness is low, the cutting is easy but the surface roughness is poor, and the workpiece is easily deformed and damaged. When the material hardness is η = 50%-60%, the cutting performance is best. sections.text: Temper brittleness: When tempering at low temperatures, if the cooling rate is too fast, the surface hardness is not high enough, and the core hardness is too high. The brittleness of the steel increases with the increase in tempering temperature. The brittleness of the steel is related to the composition of the steel, the cooling rate after tempering, and the structure of the steel. The brittleness of the steel is not a fixed property of the steel, and the hardness of the steel can have a certain effect on the brittleness.

Temper brittleness: The brittleness of the steel is not a fixed property of the steel. It is mainly related to the composition of the steel, the cooling rate after tempering, and the structure of the steel. The brittleness of the steel is not a fixed property of the steel, and the hardness of the steel can have a certain effect on the brittleness.

Reversible temper brittleness: When the temperature is raised during the tempering process, the organizational structure of the steel changes, making the steel more brittle at high temperatures. The brittleness of the steel is a reversible property. If the steel is cooled slowly after tempering, the brittleness can be eliminated. This property is mainly related to the composition of the steel.

Irreversible temper brittleness: When the steel is tempered at a certain temperature and then cooled, the brittleness of the steel increases. This brittleness cannot be eliminated by reheating. The brittleness is mainly related to the composition of the steel and the cooling rate after tempering. The brittleness of the steel is an irreversible property.

Quenching and tempering brittleness: When the steel is quenched and tempered, the brittleness of the steel increases. This brittleness is mainly related to the composition of the steel and the cooling rate after quenching. The brittleness of the steel can be reduced by tempering at a higher temperature.

Dimensional stability: The dimensional stability of the steel is related to the composition of the steel and the heat treatment process. The dimensional stability of the steel is an important property for precision parts.

Quenching and tempering brittleness: When the steel is quenched at a certain temperature and then cooled, the brittleness of the steel increases. This brittleness is mainly related to the composition of the steel and the cooling rate after quenching. The brittleness of the steel can be reduced by tempering at a higher temperature. When the temperature is between 250-400°C, the brittleness of the steel increases. When the temperature is between 250-400°C, the brittleness of the steel is the highest. When the temperature is between 350-500°C, the brittleness of the steel decreases. The brittleness of the steel is mainly related to the composition of the steel.

Decarburization sensitivity: The decarburization of the steel is related to the composition of the steel and the heat treatment process. The decarburization of the steel can cause the surface hardness to decrease and the brittleness to increase. The decarburization of the steel is an important factor affecting the quality of the steel.

Hydrogen embrittlement sensitivity: When the steel is in contact with hydrogen during the heat treatment process, the hydrogen can penetrate into the steel and cause the steel to become brittle. This brittleness is mainly related to the composition of the steel and the hydrogen content in the steel. The brittleness of the steel can be reduced by heating the steel at a higher temperature to remove the hydrogen.

Quenching crack sensitivity: When the steel is quenched, the brittleness of the steel increases due to the rapid cooling. The brittleness of the steel is mainly related to the composition of the steel and the cooling rate during quenching. The brittleness of the steel can be reduced by tempering at a higher temperature. For steels with high carbon content (Cr steel, Cr-Ni steel, Cr-Mo steel) at 450-575°C or higher temperature, the quenching crack sensitivity is high. For steels with lower carbon content at 250-400°C, the quenching crack sensitivity is lower. For steels with medium carbon content at 350-500°C, the quenching crack sensitivity is medium. The quenching crack sensitivity is mainly related to the composition of the steel.

sections.text: Problem and Explanation

The original heat treatment requirement for 40Cr-G52 (gear section) is that the high frequency induction heating should have multiple characteristics, affected by equipment accuracy, hardness, and structural shape. The production process is limited. The worm gear pair should not use through-hardening equipment (such as 250kHz high frequency, 80kHz medium frequency) to avoid similar deformation and hardness variation.

If the design specifies using 20Cr-S-G59 (20Cr carburizing, high frequency heating, 59HRC) or 40Cr-D500 (40Cr, carburizing, hardness 500HV) or 20Cr-D600 (20Cr carburizing, hardness 600HV), this raises the question: what is the requirement to reach 2.5? High frequency induction heating 52HRC meets, 20Cr carburizing 59HRC meets, carburizing 500-600HV range. However, carburizing has effective depth DN without clear requirements, making it unclear whether the design is correct for the technical requirements in this specification.

The use of different processes for each work piece has its own characteristics, and should be selected based on the steel type (such as carburizing suitable for gas nitriding, with maximum hardness) to meet the requirements. The second type uses a certain type of steel for the work piece, and its hardness and hardness value are the heat treatment technical requirements, with hardness as the main method. There are several common hardness values in heat treatment, and the method is not the same, suitable for different combinations. The second type has no clear requirements in the front part, and the method is not clear, suitable for different combinations.

For each work piece of a certain type, the size and shape are not fixed, hardness or hardness value is deep, also has, for one measurement method of the surface hardness has a certain precision. Heat treatment technical requirements should prevent the standard industry sample, ensure the heat treatment technical requirements are met, and prevent the work piece from being out of tolerance. The heat treatment technical requirements should have certain precision in the heat treatment process, and there is a certain standard in the heat treatment process, which should be referred to.

sections.text: Chapter 7 Surface Technology
1 Classification and Function of Surface Technology
1.1 Definition and Classification of Surface Technology

Surface technology is a mechanical, physical or chemical method to change the surface state of a workpiece, perform chemical decomposition, organize structural changes to respond to stress states, or add a layer of coating to make the workpiece surface have certain special properties and achieve specific application requirements.

sections.caption: Classification and Function of Surface Technology
sections.description: A comprehensive hierarchical flowchart showing the classification of surface technology. The chart branches from 'Surface Technology' into three main categories: Surface Modification (表面改性), Surface Treatment (表面处理), and Composite Surface Technology (复合表面技术). Each category further subdivides into multiple specific techniques and processes. Surface Modification includes chemical vapor deposition, physical vapor deposition, and gas phase deposition methods. Surface Treatment includes mechanical treatment, chemical treatment, electrochemical treatment, and thermal treatment methods. The chart lists numerous specific processes including nitriding, carburizing, boriding, ion implantation, various coating methods (PVD, CVD, thermal spraying, electroplating, electroless plating), and other specialized surface treatment techniques. The flowchart uses connecting lines to show relationships between different processes and their subcategories.

sections.text: 2.5 Heat Treatment of Magnesium Alloys

The conventional heat treatment process for magnesium alloys is divided into two categories: stress relief annealing (removing internal stress and complete recrystallization annealing) and solution treatment. ① The purpose of stress relief annealing is to eliminate internal stress generated during the forming process, reduce the degree of work hardening, shorten the annealing time, and improve the properties of the subsequent work. The annealing temperature is lower than the recrystallization temperature, and the annealing time is short. ② The purpose of complete recrystallization annealing is to eliminate internal stress, harden and improve the properties of the subsequent work, and the annealing temperature is higher than the recrystallization temperature, and the annealing time is long. For alloys that do not require stress relief, it is necessary to select the appropriate heat treatment process according to the performance requirements. ③ For wrought magnesium alloys such as AZ91, ZM5, and ZM6, after solution treatment, to improve the strength and hardness and prevent the precipitation of secondary phases, solid solution treatment should be performed, and the heating temperature and time should be extended. ④ For wrought magnesium alloys such as MB15, artificial aging can be performed to obtain the desired aging effect. If Mg-Zn series alloys are heated and treated, the aging effect is not ideal, and artificial aging is not suitable. The aging treatment can improve the service performance of the alloy, reduce the creep, and is mainly used for Mg-Al-Zn series and Mg-RE-Zn series.

The main characteristic of magnesium alloy heat treatment is that the dissolution and aging treatment time is long, which is an important factor in the diffusion of alloying elements. sections.text: Characteristics and Applications of Metal Coating Layers

sections.caption: Table 1.7-13
rows: Nickel plating in dry air at medium temperature is stable and does not change color. In water and humid air, it is composed of two-oxide carbide, which can be used to form a protective film. Nickel coating is generally required to be pure nickel treatment. In high temperature or high salt spray environment, nickel coating or nickel salt spray corrosion can be prevented. For special applications with thin walls (wall thickness < 0.5mm) and high mechanical strength requirements, nickel-iron alloys are often used. Nickel plating standard electrode potential is very negative, so nickel coating has multiple gold-plated barrier properties.
Used in large-scale parts and other good environmental conditions for ferrous parts, generally used for nickel plating, but not suitable for parts with nickel coating

Compared with silver plating, it has good air tightness, corrosion resistance, good lubricity, and is easy to absorb in the middle of the coating. In acidic and alkaline environments, the coating quality is poor, and the coating has poor hydrogen brittleness. In a certain potential range, the coating has a certain electrical conductivity. sections.text: 5 Composite Electroplating

Composite electroplating is an electrochemical method that allows metal (or alloy) and solid particles (or fibers) to co-deposit, thereby obtaining composite coating materials. The process is also called co-deposition. This type of composite material is called a composite electroplated layer. Its two components are: one part is a metal or alloy formed by electrochemical reaction, commonly referred to as the metal matrix; the other part is particles or fibers that do not participate in the electrochemical reaction, commonly referred to as the dispersed phase or reinforcing phase. Therefore, composite electroplated layers are composed of a metal matrix and dispersed particles, which together form a whole. The metal matrix and dispersed particles are mechanically mixed, but the resulting composite electroplated layer has certain metal properties. The composite electroplated layer has certain metal properties and does not have the properties of a single metal or alloy.

sections.text: 6 (Electroplating) Brush Plating

Brush plating is a special electroplating method. It does not use a plating tank, but uses a brush soaked in special plating solution to plate and work piece relative motion, through the brush surface to obtain the plating layer process. During work, the work piece is the cathode of the brush electrode, the brush is the anode, and the brush is loaded with plating solution. The metal ions in the plating solution are released and deposited on the work piece, and the plating layer is continuously formed. If the work piece is the anode, the brush is the cathode, a brush plating device is used to perform electrochemistry. The brush plating is a method that can form various types of surface shapes and work requirements. The plating solution has high metal ion concentration and storage convenience, safe operation, simple equipment, low cost, easy to carry, same set of equipment can plate various base metals, alloys and composite layers, and can perform electroplating and chemical treatment on certain work pieces. It does not use electrolytic bath loss of current efficiency (maximum 500A/dm²), so brush plating speed is 5-50 times faster than ordinary electroplating. The plating layer quality is uniform and controllable. Brush plating is generally not suitable for large-scale production. This method is suitable for repair and field recovery, especially for large workpieces, no need to disassemble small parts, can carry special equipment, save cost, avoid welding defects unsuitable for large area coverage.

sections.text: 8 Thermal Spraying

Thermal spraying utilizes heat supplied by fuel gas combustion, electric arc, etc., and through high-speed (strip) or non-strip state coating material is heated to a softened or molten state, then sprayed at high speed to form a coating on the surface of the workpiece. The method of forming a coating on the surface of the workpiece.

The characteristics of this technology are: (1) the coating layer is not affected by the coating work material, and the coating material can have metal and non-metal compounds, self-fused alloys (including refractory metals, tungsten, iron-based self-fused alloys), ceramic materials (including metal oxides, carbides, nitrides, borides and silicides), polymers and composite materials; (2) the coating material has a wide range of choices; (3) the coating thickness can be 0.1mm, much larger than electroplating and other coating methods, can achieve air-tight protection of gas-tight coating materials, can work in the field; (4) the coating layer quality can be controlled, the coating layer thickness can be adjusted, the coating layer can be adjusted to avoid the various problems caused by the coating process, such as hydrogen embrittlement; (5) the coating speed is high, the number of workpieces per hour can reach 50kg; (6) the coating material utilization rate is high (spray and particle separation is not easy to remove), and can be controlled, so the coating work can avoid the various problems caused by the coating process, such as hydrogen embrittlement; (7) the coating can be shaped, that is, the coating can be shaped on the surface of the substrate, so that the coating can be removed after coating, and the coating can be shaped into a shape; (8) the coating layer quality can be controlled, the coating layer thickness can be adjusted, the coating layer can be adjusted to avoid the various problems caused by the coating process, such as hydrogen embrittlement; (9) the coating material utilization rate is high, the coating material loss is small, the coating material loss is small, in this case the coating material can be used repeatedly.

The quality and coating layer performance of thermal spraying are closely related to the spraying material, spraying method and related parameters, and the spraying work surface control situation and use environment selection are important factors affecting the coating quality.

Due to the excellent material properties, simple process, thermal spraying technology is widely used in various fields of work. sections.text: 9 Plastic Powder Thermal Spray Coating

Plastic powder thermal spray coating is a metal substrate surface spray coating method that covers the metal substrate surface with a plastic coating layer, making it have the various properties of the metal substrate itself, such as mechanical properties and electrical properties, as well as the unique properties of the plastic itself, such as friction, wear resistance, corrosion resistance, high insulation, etc. This is a new type of process. Using this process, when there is a need for this type of property in the same time, it can improve product quality and efficiency, save resources and energy, and reduce environmental pollution and other surface treatment has great significance.

The spray coating methods and principles are shown in 1-7-36. When designing, it is necessary to select the appropriate method according to the characteristics of each method, considering the possible defects of the spray coating, the quality of the coating material cannot determine the coating layer, and due to the different construction methods, the same material may achieve different results.

sections.text: The coating has certain wear resistance under high-speed friction conditions. It is related to the hardness of the coating layer, the strength, internal stress, and friction coefficient of the nano particle composite coating layer. The wear resistance of the nano particle composite coating layer is related to the electroplating process parameters (voltage, current, temperature, relative motion speed, etc.), the substrate surface type, and the nano particle content. Figure 4 shows the relationship between the friction wear loss and the nano particle content in the n-Al₂O₃/Ni composite coating layer. The friction wear loss decreases with increasing nano particle content. When the nano particle content in the coating is 20g/L, the n-Al₂O₃/Ni composite coating layer has good friction wear resistance. As the nano particle content increases, the friction wear loss increases. The relative friction wear resistance is 1, and the following are the relative friction wear resistance properties of various nano particle composite coating layers.
Friction wear resistance analysis

One kind, a certain amount of nano particle can effectively improve the friction wear resistance of the nano particle composite coating layer. The nano particle can resist the friction wear resistance of the composite coating layer. The influence of the friction wear resistance can be expressed as follows: 1. The nano particle in the coating can obtain the composite coating layer to form a metal-ceramic composite structure. The addition of small particles increases the hardness and strength of the coating, and improves the friction wear resistance. 2. The composite coating layer has a large amount of nano particles distributed in the coating, which can reduce the friction wear resistance. However, when the liquid in the nano particle composite coating is too high, the friction wear resistance ability decreases. Due to the electroplating liquid dispersion ability limitation, the nano particle in the electroplating liquid cannot be evenly distributed in the nano particle composite coating, resulting in the nano particle content increase, the friction wear resistance ability decreases. There is such a critical point in the friction wear resistance, which needs to be deeply studied.

Safety layer thickness is the reference layer thickness under the condition of ensuring multiple performance indicators. Under the premise of ensuring safety layer thickness, once the thickness exceeds the safety layer thickness, the load-bearing capacity increases, the friction coefficient increases, and the overall strength decreases. Single-layer exceeding thickness will cause application layer increase and cladding layer peeling. Therefore, it must be limited to single-layer thickness. Different coatings also have a comparative safety thickness, as shown in Table 1-7-23.

In order to meet the requirements of cladding surface recovery for small-size workpieces, it is necessary to change the cladding layer's force distribution and prevent application in one direction from increasing to more than the cladding layer and the body's bonding force, causing cladding layer peeling. The core cladding layer's main function is to distribute the force of the variable cladding layer, prevent application in one direction from increasing to more than the cladding layer and the body's bonding force. The core cladding layer's safety thickness is generally not less than 0.05mm.

Single-layer safety thickness and cladding accumulation have a large relationship. For example, a fine steel bar with a groove (length × width × depth: 200mm × 3mm × 1mm) can use a certain cladding liquid once without using core cladding.

Nano-composite electroplating technology is a new technology developed on the basis of electroplating technology. It is a combination of nano-materials and electroplating technology, not only maintaining the advantages of electroplating, but also greatly expanding the application range of electroplating, improving the application effect, and it is not only a surface treatment technology, but also a key technology for related applications.

Shot Peening Principles and Applications

sections.caption: Table 1-7-43
rows: Using compressed air to drive shot peening through a nozzle at high speed, impacting the metal surface. Using the impact of shot peening and friction on the metal surface, combined with subsequent cleaning, to remove oxide scale and rust on the aluminum alloy surface.
To prevent fatigue failure of the contact layer structure

Using pressure gas (or centrifugal force) to accelerate shot (generally steel shot, diameter 0.8-1.2mm, hardness 47-50HRC) to impact the metal surface. Using the impact of shot peening, the shape changes 0.1-0.3mm, the surface is hardened, forming a certain depth of residual compressive stress layer, which can significantly improve the fatigue strength of the work surface. The residual compressive stress layer depth and magnitude depend on the shot peening parameters. At the same time, the surface roughness increases, the surface hardness increases, and the fatigue strength is improved. The shot peening strengthening effect is better than other surface hardening methods. Shot peening can also be used for deburring and surface cleaning. The shot peening strengthening effect is not changed by the work surface state control. Shot peening strengthening is generally used for bending and torsion, and for compression without bending, the shot peening is performed on the back surface.

Using shot peening to improve the fatigue strength of work surfaces. For most shot peening applications, the maximum stress should not exceed the yield strength. After shot peening, the surface roughness increases, and the fatigue strength can be improved. For colored metals, non-ferrous metals, cast iron and cast steel, shot peening can be used. After shot peening, the surface roughness can be reduced to Ra 6.3-3.2μm by polishing.

rows: It is a laser remelting-based surface modification technology that adds some alloy elements, refractory materials and alloying elements to the laser cladding area through laser heating and melting, achieving the desired alloy composition. The alloy elements added are based on the substrate and differ from the substrate alloy composition. The use of alloy powder particles will remain in the alloy matrix. From the surface appearance of the coating and the hardness improvement, laser cladding can form a coating with high hardness and cold hardness. This type of hardness transition is smooth, the coating structure is fine, and the hardness can be increased by a small amount under the condition of maintaining high hardness of the coating layer. The method has no defects or cannot obtain the alloy coating with the required hardness. Laser cladding is used to create alloy coatings that provide manufacturers with possible applications.

It is the use of laser shock waves at high intensity on the material surface. The shock wave generated by the laser can reach 10⁴ MPa. In this case, the surface material undergoes plastic deformation, and the surface layer material shows strong hardness. The shock hardening can greatly improve the surface hardness and fatigue strength. Practice has shown that using laser 7075 aluminum alloy for shock hardening can increase the surface hardness by 3 (left and right), and the hardness can be greatly improved. The aluminum alloy structure of the weld seam can use laser shock hardening to restore the hardness of the material.

It is a high-speed impact laser shock wave located at a position directly opposite to the material surface, causing the material surface to generate heat (T = 10⁴K), evaporation, electrical discharge, plasma formation, sputtering, and other phenomena. In the sublayer film deposition, the pulsed laser shock wave can be used to deposit a thin film. The PLD coating method is easy to control the temperature (such as room temperature) and can be used for multi-element compound films. It is suitable for coating materials with different melting points. The method has the advantages of simple operation, easy control of film thickness, and easy development of coating materials. The method has the disadvantages of long processing time and limited application prospects.

It is a transmission laser cleaning technology based on the principle of laser ablation. Using laser beam irradiation to remove rust and dirt on the surface, or using laser beam irradiation to generate high-temperature heat, causing uneven heating and thermal stress, causing the surface coating to peel off or fall off. The purpose is to achieve the goal of cleaning the work surface. Through high-power laser irradiation, laser ablation, and laser cleaning, the work surface is cleaned. The laser cleaning technology is widely used in industry, and it is a non-contact cleaning method that is environmentally friendly and safe.

It is a process that uses laser shock wave accumulation (PLD) technology to perform shock hardening on the surface of the material. When laser shock wave acts on the surface of the material, it produces a temperature rise and heat conduction, causing the material to undergo plastic deformation and hardening. This is a process that combines gas shock waves with the material surface. The shock wave can reach 10 mm, with high hardness and no brittle fracture. In this process, laser shock is required to be performed on the material surface. Depending on the material requirements, laser shock hardening can be used to test the material.

sections.text: 10 Steel Iron Control Parts Powder Zinc Plating (Extracted from JB/T 5067—1999)

Powder zinc plating is a method of using the original powder infiltration principle to coat zinc onto work pieces with zinc and copper alloys, forming a zinc-copper alloy coating on the metal zinc and work pieces at the same time. The zinc electrons are scattered to the work piece center, forming a zinc-plated layer. The method of complete zinc plating is used: ① to prevent zinc powder agglomeration and help zinc powder distribution; ② to have zinc on the work piece to heat; ③ to prevent work piece deformation during heating. At present, powder zinc plating is widely used in springs, fasteners, and other parts that require high-temperature resistance control.
Powder zinc plating is used for steel, low carbon steel, 45 steel, 16Mn, spring steel, cast iron, white iron and other materials for small parts.
(1) Characteristics

The zinc layer is uniformly distributed, which can ensure that the zinc layer has mechanical properties and has a zinc-infiltrated layer that can reach the required hardness. The zinc layer thickness can reach the thermal hardening standard specified in the specification.

The zinc layer combined with the substrate has a certain adhesion strength. It can be used at 400~500°C temperature range. At 350HV hardness, the thermal fatigue resistance of the zinc layer is good. The zinc layer hardness is not equal to the conditions under the zinc-infiltrated layer, and the ratio is as high as thermal zinc-plated layer of about 35%.
The zinc layer surface can be directly coated or covered with other materials, without special treatment after the combination is fixed.

The zinc layer surface should be free of obvious dirt, rust, oxidation layer, etc. The zinc layer surface should be smooth and bright, without light spots; after chemical and mechanical polishing, the surface should be bright and smooth, with metallic luster, and the zinc layer should have a metallic luster.

Surface Nanocrystallization

sections.caption: Table 1-7-49
rows: Nanocrystalline metals and alloys are mainly produced by rapid cooling, rapid solidification, severe plastic deformation, and chemical methods. Due to the ultra-fine grain structure and chemical composition of nanocrystalline materials, they exhibit unique physical and chemical properties. Compared with conventional coarse-grained materials, nanocrystalline materials have higher strength, hardness, and elastic modulus, lower density, lower melting point, higher diffusion rate, and better corrosion resistance. In addition, the surface nanocrystallization can significantly improve the fatigue strength and wear resistance of materials.

Surface nanocrystallization of metals and alloys can be achieved through methods such as severe plastic deformation, rapid cooling and solidification, mechanical alloying, surface mechanical attrition treatment, and other advanced technologies. In recent years, with the development of surface technology, surface nanocrystallization has been widely used in industrial applications. By using high-energy ball milling, surface mechanical attrition treatment, and other methods, it is possible to achieve surface nanocrystallization. The goal is to utilize advanced surface technology to achieve surface nanocrystallization and improve the service life of components.

sections.text: 15 Coating

Coating is the use of organic materials to coat a certain method to protect the surface of materials, forming a coating film that is part of the coating process. The organic materials used for coating can coat the material surface to form a protective layer, decorative special properties (such as gloss, waterproof, anti-corrosion, etc.). The solid coating is a class of liquid or solid material of the total name. Early large numbers of plant oils are important raw materials, so there is "oil paint" name, later synthetic resin gradually replaced plant oil, because it is collectively called "coating", in addition to showing obvious characteristics of specific coating materials can be called "lacquer", other non-lacquer materials cannot be called "lacquer".

Composition, Characteristics and Comparison of High-Energy Beam Surface Strengthening Technology

High-energy beam surface strengthening technology uses 10³ J/W·cm² or higher power density high-energy beam to concentrate on the metal surface. Through surface scanning or random irradiation with auxiliary materials, the metal surface undergoes rapid heating, melting, vaporization, and chemical reactions of metal oxides, nitrides, and carbides, achieving changes in surface composition and structure. This technology includes electron beam surface strengthening technology, laser beam surface strengthening technology, and others. The high-energy beam provides energy sources including: laser, electron beam, ion beam, electric arc, and ultrasonic waves. As shown in the table:

It can also be used for surface alloying, cladding, hardening, and other treatments. It can also be used for surface cleaning, derusting, and other purposes.

It is a process in which ions from an ion source are implanted into the surface of a solid material. The ions are accelerated and injected into the material surface at high speed.
