2.1 Selection of Benchmark System

When selecting the benchmark system, the structure, process, and economic aspects should be comprehensively considered. (1) For parts with size tolerance (500mm or less), it is generally preferable to select the benchmark system. This can reduce the number of knives, the number of tools, and be more economical. (2) The benchmark system is often used for the following situations:

items: a. The public difference level of the matching surface should not be too high (generally HR or higher), or use cold-drawn rods (generally not exceeding the size) to make shafts, and also add processing.

b. According to Figure 2-2-1 shown structure, use active shaft and active shaft to require the fit to be a passive fit, and the shaft with the hole should be processed into a shaft, this is more convenient, and the benchmark system is used on one side, the active shaft is processed into a shaft, the shaft pair is made into a small amount of fit, which is convenient.
c. Each part of the same benchmark size requires the upper and lower fit conditions.

sections.text: (3) When matching with the benchmark system, the selection of the benchmark is usually based on the benchmark surface. For example, when matching the rolling shaft with the benchmark system, the shaft is pressed into the hole, and the rolling shaft bears the hole combined with the hole pressed by the benchmark system. If the benchmark is not clear, in order to meet the special requirements of the fit, it is not recommended to use the combined fit. For example, M7, K8/k6, etc., the fit number is not H or h, the mixed fit uses one hole (or shaft) and several shafts (or holes) combined fit. sections.text: 2.3 Selection of Matching
The selection of matching should focus on the following points:

items: ① Working conditions of matching parts (refer to Table 2-2-10).

a. Relative motion conditions: For matching parts with relative motion, the direction of relative motion should be selected. When the speed is large in one direction and small in the other direction, the relative motion time is long, the matching should be selected to pass through the clearance or transition matching.
b. Load conditions: Generally, if the bearing pressure is large in one direction, in static loading or light dynamic loading, the maximum clearance is allowed.

c. Precision requirements: If precision requirements are high, transition matching should be selected, and the basic hole system or basic shaft system can be used. If precision requirements are not high, the basic hole system can be used, or the basic shaft system can be used.

d. Disassembly conditions: For parts with relative motion, frequent disassembly, use of a or b combination matching, no special requirements for dynamic disassembly, generally use a, h or j, or k combination matching. If not disassembled during assembly, use k combination matching, basically not disassembled, use m or n combination matching. When the machine has internal space constraints, in order to facilitate matching of parts, it is necessary to ensure that the parts are not disassembled on the machine, and the working conditions must be met, and the matching should be selected through large clearance matching.
e. Working temperature: When the working temperature of matching parts is significantly different from the assembly temperature, the matching must be selected to work at the temperature change.

f. High temperature and low temperature conditions below working temperature (-60~800°C), if the matching material has a linear expansion coefficient difference, the matching clearance (or transition) should be used for positive calculation. Refer to Section 4.

③ Production accuracy of matching parts: Single small batch production, holes with tolerance close to the lower limit, shafts with tolerance close to the upper limit, resulting in hole-shaft matching gaps. Due to reciprocal response to clearance, some clearance is allowed.

④ Application of standard or non-standard matching: Refer to Tables 2-2-43, 2-2-44. For satisfying the matching of special requirements, allowing the use of non-standard matching. For dimensions exceeding the standard (greater than 500mm), public tolerance level matching of small batch production should be used, should be selected to use interchangeable production. When ordinary methods are difficult to meet accuracy requirements, can use matching (GB/T 1801-2009).
⑤ Geometric tolerance: Position tolerance difference table surface should be relative to the matching quality.

⑥ Selection of transition matching: Due to the influence of small matching quality on the transition matching, the comparison is more sensitive. Therefore, it is necessary to comprehensively consider multiple factors, such as the diameter of the matching, length, working material properties, surface roughness, geometric tolerance, matching position, and the application of assembly and matching methods. Refer to Section 2-2-9.

sections.text: 3 General Tolerances: Linear and Angular Dimensions Tolerances Not Indicated (Excerpted from GB/T 1804—2000)
3.1 Concept of General Tolerances for Linear and Angular Dimensions

① General tolerance is a tolerance applied to dimensions that do not have a tolerance value specified under the condition of ensuring the tolerance of the part. Using the general tolerance of the dimension, the tolerance value is not indicated on the drawing, and the tolerance grade is determined by the standard. It is applicable to metal cutting and machining. It is used for general machining accuracy. The standard applies to the following dimensions: linear dimensions, such as length, width, height, thickness, diameter, radius, distance, and taper angle; angular dimensions, including general angular dimensions not indicated in the drawing, such as angles (90°), GB/T 1184 provided or other polygonal angular dimensions; machine tool fixture linear and angular dimensions.

② The standard does not apply to the following dimensions: other general tolerance standards involving linear and angular dimensions; dimensions within the scope of reference frames; distance from the reference frame to the theoretical dimension.

Select the general tolerance grade from the drawing of the general tolerance dimension, considering the normal vehicle body accuracy and corresponding technical documents or standards for specific provisions.

For a first-class dimension, if the upper and lower tolerances are not equal or the tolerance is larger than the general tolerance, the relative tolerance limit deviation should be indicated on the drawing. When the dimension is not indicated on the drawing, the tolerance should be marked according to section 3.3 of the standard.

Due to different types of processes (such as turning and milling), the unindicated tolerance of the two surfaces of the part should be controlled by the maximum tolerance value in the two general tolerance values.

The direction of the linear element controlled by the general tolerance should not control the direction of the form deviation. From the actual surface to the line of the total direction is the ideal direction of the form deviation. The line and the actual line in the direction of the maximum deviation should be as small as possible (see GB/T 4249).

② The tolerance of the tolerance is the tolerance and shape of the dimension. Due to the tolerance deviation of the dimension from the form deviation, the form deviation of the part is used to ensure that the part can be used normally. Therefore, the tolerance in the sample table shows all the tolerance requirements.

③ The general tolerance of linear and angular dimensions is applied under the condition of normal passage through the process. The machine tool equipment can ensure the tolerance of the dimension. In the normal maintenance and operation situation, the tolerance value of the general tolerance is consistent with the tolerance level. According to the tolerance level used, the corresponding general tolerance should be selected.

Linear dimensions of general tolerance are mainly used for low-precision matching dimensions. Using the general tolerance of the dimension in the normal tolerance level ensures that the part is not checked. For the specified general tolerance, the maximum deviation is not greater than the general tolerance. For example, for a 35mm diameter hole, the specification is 1mm of the tolerance limit deviation, and the use of ±0.3mm general tolerance limit deviation (medium grade) is sufficient.

When the tolerance of the dimension is greater than or less than the general tolerance, the general tolerance should be used. Only when the tolerance of the part is allowed to exceed the general tolerance, the corresponding tolerance limit deviation value should be indicated on the drawing.

④ When the tolerance of the dimension is greater than the general tolerance, the tolerance should be indicated on the drawing. The tolerance should be indicated on the drawing (such as the tolerance indicated by the tolerance frame), and the corresponding tolerance limit deviation value should be indicated on the drawing.

⑤ The tolerance of the tolerance is usually a general tolerance. When the work task is exceeded (such as ground processing), the general tolerance of the work task is not restricted. Only when the tolerance of the part is allowed to be affected, the general tolerance of the work task is not restricted.

4 Calculation of assembly clearance under high temperature or low temperature working conditions

The dimensions marked on the working drawing are based on the standard temperature of 20°C. However, some machinery such as machine tools, aircraft, and aero-engines may work at temperatures of 800°C to -60°C or other high or low temperature conditions. If the expansion coefficient of the material is different, the assembly clearance (or interference) needs to be corrected and calculated according to the temperature change. The calculation formula is as follows:
x_max = x_Gmax + d[α_s(t_s - t) ∓ α_k(t_k - t)]
x_min = x_Gmin + d[α_s(t_s - t) ∓ α_k(t_k - t)]

In the formula: x_max, x_min—maximum and minimum assembly clearance, mm; t_k, t_s—working temperature of the hole and shaft, °C; x_Gmax, x_Gmin—maximum and minimum assembly clearance at standard temperature, mm; t—standard temperature, °C; d—nominal diameter of the assembly, mm; α_k, α_s—linear expansion coefficient of the hole and shaft material, °C⁻¹.

In formulas (2-2-1) and (2-2-2), the negative sign applies when the temperature is high, and the hole diameter expands more than the shaft diameter (if the hole diameter is larger than the shaft diameter at high temperature, the local clearance increases, and the small hole with high temperature is smaller than the hole without heating). The positive sign applies when the temperature is low and the hole diameter shrinks less than the shaft diameter (if the hole diameter is smaller than the shaft diameter at low temperature, the local clearance decreases).

Example: The hole and shaft have a nominal diameter of d = 150 mm, working temperature t_k = 110°C, t_s = 180°C, α_k = 12×10⁻⁶°C⁻¹, α_s = 24×10⁻⁶°C⁻¹, standard temperature t = 20°C. Calculate the assembly clearance.

5.1.4 Circular runout tolerance values

(1) Circular runout tolerance Tp
The nominal diameter (generally the maximum circular runout diameter D) is used as the nominal size, and the standard circular runout tolerance is selected according to GB/T 1800.1—2009.

(2) Circular runout tolerance of the datum surface Tpre
The diameter d is used as the nominal size, and the standard circular runout tolerance is selected according to GB/T 1800.1—2009.

(3) Circular runout tolerance AT
① Circular runout tolerance AT is divided into 12 tolerance grades, represented by AT1, AT2, ..., AT12. The circular runout tolerance values are shown in Table 2-2-50. When the tolerance grade of the datum surface is required, the tolerance band width is used as the circular runout tolerance.

When higher or lower tolerance grades of circular runout tolerance are required, according to the ratio of 1.6 between adjacent tolerance grades, higher grades such as AT0, AT01 are shown, and lower grades such as AT13, AT14 are shown.

② Circular runout tolerance can be expressed in two forms:
a. ATa—expressed in diameter and position strength value, in minutes and seconds;
b. ATD—expressed in length and position tolerance.
The relationship between ATa and ATD is:
ATa = ATD × 10^-3

In the formula, ATD has a unit of μm; ATa has a unit of μrad; L has a unit of mm.
ATD is calculated according to the formula in Table 2-2-50, which gives the ATD range value corresponding to the nominal diameter L in Table 2-2-50. The ATD calculation result is rounded according to GB/T 8170, and the effective number of digits corresponds to the maximum circular runout tolerance value in Table 2-2-50.

Example: L is 50mm, using AT7, check Table 2-2-50 for ATa is 315μrad or 1.05°, then
ATD = ATa × 10^-3 = 315 × 50 × 10^-3
= 15.75 (μm)
Take ATD = 15.8μm.

Circular runout tolerance limit deviation is expressed as a single direction or bidirectional (symmetrical or asymmetrical) value (Figure 2-2-10).

T_E = E_max - E_min = (1/C)|Y_max - Y_min|
In the formula: C — stiffness; Y_max — maximum load of the fit; Y_min — minimum load of the fit.
5.2.4 Calculation of Radial Runout Error of Inner and Outer Circular Grooves

The radial runout error of a circular groove axis is the radial runout between a reference groove and its corresponding groove axis position, as shown in Figure 2-2-11. The radial runout error of the outer groove relative to the upper axis is e_s2, ES_2; the radial runout error of the inner groove relative to the lower axis is e_i1, EI_1. sections.text: (2) Comprehensive consideration of shape, position, and three types of tolerance relationships
① Reasonable consideration of the relationship between shape and position tolerances

In the first step, the shape tolerance should be given to the form tolerance value that is smaller than the position tolerance difference. For example, if two parallel surfaces have a flatness tolerance, the flatness tolerance value should be smaller than the parallelism tolerance value. The shape tolerance of cylindrical parts (excluding the axis line) is generally smaller than the diameter tolerance. The parallelism tolerance should be smaller than the corresponding distance tolerance.
② According to the functional requirements of the part, select appropriate tolerance principles. See Tables 2-3-15 and 2-3-16.

For dimensional tolerances and positional tolerances that require separation of the tolerance zone, two different elements must be used, and the independent principle should be adopted. For dimensional tolerances and positional tolerances that do not require separation of the tolerance zone, the relevant requirements should be used, and the related principle should be adopted. When the dimensional tolerance and positional tolerance have different requirements, use the principle of related requirements, and according to the actual needs, use the principle of related requirements, and according to the actual needs of the design, use the principle of related requirements. When the measured size is the maximum actual size (i.e., the actual body shape under the maximum body condition), control it, and use the packaging requirement.

sections.text: ③ Selection of position of φ60D8 holes on both ends

The two holes are the thrust shaft holes. To ensure that the hole surface and the thrust force on the shaft are in contact, avoid eccentric surface radial runout, and meet any coaxiality requirements.

For the selection of radial runout of the end face, according to the coaxiality tolerance level of the hole, the radial runout tolerance level of the corresponding end face can be determined. See Table 2-3-21. For the radial runout tolerance level of the end face, the corresponding radial runout tolerance of 7 levels is ≤7 levels. See Table 2-3-24, the tolerance value is 0.025mm.
④ Selection of perpendicularity tolerance of the end face

To ensure that the shaft runs true on the upper and lower vertical surfaces, the shaft must be a straight φ80h5 shaft line. All requirements must be met with vertical tolerance to ensure perpendicularity. For the selection of perpendicularity tolerance of the vertical line, according to the inspection tolerance of the shaft, the perpendicularity tolerance level can be 6 levels (IT6). The end face perpendicularity tolerance level is 8 levels (ITS) with tolerance value ≤7 levels. See Table 2-3-20, the 8-level tolerance value corresponding to the vertical tolerance level is 6 levels. According to the 54mm tolerance segment, see Table 2-3-25, the tolerance value is 0.02mm. When marking on the drawing, the tolerance should be marked on the inspection rod. If the inspection tolerance is 100mm, the tolerance (also 2 times) is 0.04mm.
⑤ Selection of tooth profile dividing line coaxiality tolerance

To ensure that the shaft operates smoothly when the lower and upper gears mesh, the tooth profile dividing line structure must be parallel to the φ80h5 shaft line. All requirements must be given to ensure the vertical tolerance.

For the selection of coaxiality tolerance of the parallel position, since the same φ80h5 shaft line is used as the standard, the parallel position can be selected with the same form position coaxiality tolerance level of 6 levels. See Table 2-3-25, the tolerance value is 0.05mm.

Chapter 4 Surface Structure
1 Overview
1.1 Concept of Surface Structure

Surface structure is the surface roughness, surface waviness, surface defects, and surface form deviations of a workpiece. The various characteristics of surface structure are not independent of each other. In metal cutting and other processing, due to differences in processing methods, the geometric shape deviations of the workpiece surface vary. Surface roughness, surface waviness, and surface form deviations are three characteristic deviations that exist independently. Most surface deviations are caused by roughness, waviness, and form deviations. Due to the different effects of roughness, waviness, and form deviations on function, they can be distinguished separately (Figure 2-4-1).

sections.text: (12) Effect of surface roughness on fluid flow resistance in pipes

When fluid flows in a pipe, it is subjected to friction. When the pipe has a rough surface, the friction resistance increases. The roughness of the pipe wall ε = Rz/r (where r is the average height of the pipe wall) is used as an indicator of surface roughness. The smaller the roughness, the smaller the friction resistance and the smaller the loss of friction resistance. The friction resistance is related to the relative roughness and the flow state in the pipe. Especially, the relationship between the relative roughness and the friction coefficient is shown in Table 2-4-15.

4.2 Selection of surface roughness parameters

① For horizontal surfaces, Ra is a commonly used parameter. In the surface roughness range (Ra 0.025-6.3μm, Rz 0.1-25μm range), Ra should be preferentially used. Ra can reflect the processing characteristics of the surface and can reflect the shape characteristics to some extent. When the maximum height Rz is only able to reflect the maximum height of the surface roughness, it cannot reflect the roughness characteristics of the shape, and for some surfaces that do not allow obvious deep grooves in the processing (affecting fatigue strength) and small parts with surface (such as bearings, shafts, etc.) with specific uses, Rz should be used for evaluation. Rz and Ra are used together to control multiple functional requirements.

② For parts with specific functions, Ra and Rz are generally used to control surface roughness. For some parts with higher functional requirements, such as coating adhesion, corrosion resistance, fatigue strength, contact stiffness, etc., Rsm should be used to control the fine spacing of the surface roughness. For friction, contact stiffness, and other parts requiring higher surface quality (such as bearings, shafts, bushings, etc.), mixed parameters Rmr(c) should be used to control the surface quality. When specifying Rmr(c) values, the corresponding Rz and Ra values must be given. For detailed parameters Rsm and Rmr(c), refer to GB/T 1031-2009.
4.3 Selection of surface roughness parameter values

The selection of surface roughness parameter values should be based on the direct relationship between the parameters and the functional requirements of the parts, the quality of the product, the service life and manufacturing cost. Each part should be selected according to its functional requirements. Each surface should have a corresponding management parameter value range. Under the premise of meeting the functional requirements of the parts, the largest roughness parameter value should be used.
4 Selection of Surface Structure Parameters
4.1 Influence of Surface Roughness on Bearing Function

(1) Effect on composite bearing performance
Composite bearing requires a stable composite surface, and the bearing surface of the bearing pair should be small. It is required that the bearing surface roughness Ra value should not be too large. The public difference level should not exceed the large size (especially 1-3 level public difference level). The same public difference level shaft hole Ra value should be low. For composite bearing materials, the smaller the surface, the lower its Ra value. The same work surface roughness value should not be higher than the work surface.

(2) Effect on friction surface
The friction surface is much higher than the friction surface, the liquid friction surface is higher than the friction surface, the running speed is higher, the surface comparison is dynamic speed is lower, the unit is pressure Pa. The friction surface unit pressure force on the friction surface Ra value should be low.

(3) Effect on rough strength
The bearing surface is easy to produce stress concentration in the stress, the groove is shallow, the Ra value is low. The roughness of the part has an effect on the strength of the rough part. The effect on the steel part side strength is significant, and the effect on the steel part side strength is large.

(4) Effect on contact rigidity
When two rough surfaces are in contact, under the action of force, it is easy to produce contact deformation. Therefore, the Ra value is reduced to increase the contact rigidity of the part.

(5) Effect on impact strength
The impact strength of the part surface is reduced by the surface roughness Ra value, which is reduced at low temperature, and is not obvious.

(6) Effect on corrosion resistance
The surface roughness should be on the surface of the part. The corrosion resistance of the body or liquid body is affected by the part, and the corrosion resistance of the part surface layer is penetrated, and the corrosion resistance is increased. Therefore, the corrosion resistance of the gas body or liquid body in the working part of the surface Ra value is low.

(7) Effect on composite sealing
The surface is clean and clean. The surface is clean and has relative sliding of the sealing surface. Due to relative motion, the micro-unevenness is generally 4-5μm. Use to store sliding oil with light oil. The surface is too clean, not only can it store sliding oil, but also can cause elastic friction. Therefore, the sealing of the seal is good and the addition of directional direction is related.

(8) Effect on vibration and noise
Machine equipment running surface roughness is not flat, running at high speed will produce vibration and noise, to reduce the running friction damping, support and drive the machine shaft, the shaft and other parts, this phenomenon is more obvious, because the running surface roughness Ra value is low, the running part is smooth and noiseless.

(9) Effect on high-frequency current
When high-frequency current is in the body surface groove, the current is concentrated in the body surface 1μm deep thin layer, due to the surface roughness, the surface resistance is actually larger than the theoretical value.

(10) Effect on gold plating coating amount
Work plating, plating, plating, its surface roughness is not uniform depth ratio plating increase one-fold, and plating after, the plating is reduced by one-half. Due to the roughness of the surface, the plating is not easy to produce cracks, in the coating metal surface to use the surface has a certain roughness.

(11) Effect on measurement accuracy
Due to the surface roughness, when measuring, the measurement is actually in contact with the substrate, the measurement is not accurate, but the contact surface is small, the unit area of the small, so it is a certain contact shape. Due to the surface roughness has a certain peak rise, if the measurement, the measurement and the measured surface work relative motion, this makes the measurement is also measured by the surface peak rise on the surface, affecting the indication value has a certain effect.

Polished light is used to reduce the surface roughness, and the light is reflected back to the material on the surface. The light penetration depth is about 0.018μm. In the same steel measurement block in the English flat work measurement, for the measurement of the result should be one-to-0.018μm correction. The surface roughness for the material depth has an effect, the amount of the surface Ra value is generally 0.007-0.012μm, which makes the light penetration depth also changes. In the same set of measurement blocks relative difference can reach 0.06μm.

1 Calculation Formula for Hole Position Deviation

Hole position deviation is based on the axis (such as counterbore, double-end threaded holes, tapped holes, dowel pins, etc.) and the combined surface of the hole. When calculating hole position deviation, the general rule is to use the hole diameter in the middle of the hole. When calculating hole position deviation, the general rule is to use the hole diameter in the middle of the hole. The size of the hole position tolerance is determined by the size and position of the hole. The hole position tolerance is related to the hole size; the hole axis size is known, that is, the maximum hole size is known. The hole position tolerance is used to ensure that the hole axis can pass through the hole during assembly. In the assembly process, due to the fact that the hole axis can be offset by the hole position tolerance, the hole position deviation caused by the assembly process should be considered. When assembling, it is necessary to clarify the type of connection structure; screws (through holes), see Figure 2-5-1; dowel pins (double-end threaded holes, dowel pins, etc.), see Figure 2-5-2.
Minimum hole position s_u is:
s_u = d_0 - d
Where: d_0 — minimum limit size of hole; d — maximum limit size of axis.

When the number of holes is greater than 3, the general formula marking method is not used. Because the deviation changes with the increase in the number of holes, the number of holes is large, the hole position deviation is small, and the processing difficulty increases. If the formula marking method is used, the hole position deviation and hole number are irrelevant.

sections.text: The motion accuracy of gear teeth depends on the precision of the gear shaft. sections.text: Figure 2-6-3 shows the outline dimensions of a typical reducer housing and the dimensional, geometric tolerance, and surface roughness requirements. The housing is divided into two parts: to ensure the accuracy of the shaft bore, the two φ100H7 shaft bores are defined as the basic shaft line; the two φ90H8 holes are defined with respect to the B-C common axis line as the datum. The theoretical position of the common axis B-C is determined by the theoretical dimensions specified in the drawing. The core idea is that the position error of the common axis B-C is divided into two parts: the position error of a certain surface of a certain datum with respect to the common axis B-C, and the position error of the housing's left and right end faces with respect to the common axis A datum. The position error of the two φ90H8 holes is defined with respect to A, B-C, and D as the datum, and the position error requirement should be such that the hole axis is perpendicular to the B-C axis. The position is defined as the standard line, and the position error is defined as φ0.030mm as the datum, and the position error of the A end face with respect to the B-C axis is not more than φ0.012mm; in addition, the position of the housing's left and right end faces with respect to the A datum is defined as 0.05mm. The specific tolerance and roughness requirements are shown in Figure 2-6-3.

Ak为冲击断面的比值称为冲击韧度。按国家标准规定，aKU为比U形缺口试样冲击断裂所消耗的冲击吸收功（J）
aKV为比V形缺口试样冲击断裂所消耗的冲击吸收功（J）
由于aK值的大小不仅取决于材料本身，同时还随试样尺寸、形状的改变及试验温度的不同而改变，因而aK值只是一个相对指标。目前国际上许多国家直接采用冲击吸收功AK作为冲击韧性的指标，我国将逐步用AK代替aK

硬度是指金属抵抗硬的物体压入其表面的能力
用淬硬小钢球或硬质合金压入金属表面，保持一定时间后卸去，以其压痕面积加在钢球上的载荷，所得之值，即为金属的布氏硬度值。硬度小于或等于650HBW（见GB/T 231.1）时使用硬度合金球测定
当试验力单位为N时，布氏硬度值为
HBW = 0.102 × 2F/(πD(D-√(D²-d²))) (kgf/mm²)
式中 F——硬度合金球上的载荷，N
D——硬度合金球直径，mm
d——压痕平均直径，mm
如果试验力单位为kgf，则式中系数0.102应为1

1 Degree of Freedom Analysis of Mechanisms
1.1 Concepts of Common Terminology

sections.caption: Table 4-1-1
rows: The basic unit that constitutes the structure of a mechanism. Each component that makes up a mechanism is called a component. The relative motion between components is the basis for the mechanism to perform its function. According to the number of motion pairs, components can be divided into: binary components, ternary components, quaternary components, etc.

The component in the mechanism that is directly driven by external force or energy. It is the original input component. The motion of the active component determines the motion of other components in the mechanism. The active component is also called the input component or driving component.

A kinematic pair where the contact between the two components is a point or line. The relative motion between the two components in a high pair is a combination of rolling and sliding. High pairs have fewer constraints on the relative motion of components.

The component in the mechanism that is driven by the active component through the kinematic chain. It is the final output component. The motion of the driven component is determined by the motion of the active component and the structure of the mechanism. The driven component is also called the output component or follower.

A kinematic pair where the contact between the two components is a surface. The relative motion between the two components in a low pair is pure rolling or pure sliding. Low pairs have more constraints on the relative motion of components.

A system composed of multiple components connected by kinematic pairs. It is used to transmit motion and force. Each mechanism is composed of a fixed component (frame) and moving components. The motion of the mechanism is determined by the motion of the active component and the structure of the mechanism.
A type of motion where the components form a closed loop. The relative motion between components is constrained by the closed loop structure.
A mechanism where all components move in parallel planes. The motion of each component is confined to a plane parallel to a reference plane. Planar mechanisms are the most common type of mechanism.
A type of motion where the components do not form a closed loop. The relative motion between components is not constrained by a closed loop structure.
A mechanism where the components move in different planes. The motion of each component is not confined to a single plane. Spatial mechanisms are more complex than planar mechanisms.

The number of independent parameters needed to completely describe the position of a mechanism. It is determined by the number of components, the number of kinematic pairs, and the constraints imposed by the kinematic pairs. For example, a mechanism with n components and p kinematic pairs has a degree of freedom of F = 3(n-1) - 2p₁ - p₂, where p₁ is the number of low pairs and p₂ is the number of high pairs.

A general term for mechanisms and mechanical systems. A machine is composed of multiple mechanisms connected together to perform a specific function. Machines are used to transform energy and transmit motion and force.

sections.text: Chapter 4
5.3.3 Composition and main manufacturing methods of glass fiber reinforced plastic

Glass fiber reinforced plastic (glass fiber reinforced thermosetting plastic) is made of composite resin as the base material and glass fiber as the reinforcing material and filler. The main resins used are unsaturated polyester resin, epoxy resin, phenolic resin, and furan resin. Among them, unsaturated polyester resin is the most widely used. To adapt to different requirements, such as improving performance and reducing cost, a second type of synthetic resin is often used for modification. If unsaturated polyester glass fiber reinforced plastic is used, unsaturated epoxy glass fiber reinforced plastic, or a combination of unsaturated-epoxy composite resin is used, adding polyester resin in the resin, plasticizer, thickener, thixotropic agent and other auxiliary materials, the degree of influence on the performance of glass fiber reinforced plastic is different.

Glass fiber reinforced plastic - an important component of glass fiber reinforced plastic and glass fiber reinforced plastic. The mechanical properties of glass fiber reinforced plastic are closely related to the fiber content, type, and specifications. Due to the different properties of glass fiber reinforced plastic, except for special cases (such as fluorine-containing, alkali-resistant), the corrosion resistance of glass fiber reinforced plastic is mainly determined by the corrosion resistance of the resin.

The structural design of glass fiber reinforced plastic equipment varies depending on the manufacturing method used. The main ones are experimental and trial production. Figure 3-4-1 shows the basic structure of glass fiber reinforced plastic equipment. The glass fiber reinforced plastic layer structure is as follows:

items: Inner layer (corrosion-resistant layer): The innermost layer is composed of glass fiber cloth saturated with resin, and the innermost layer is in contact with the corrosive medium.
Middle layer: Made of glass fiber cloth saturated with resin, approximately 2mm thick, can isolate the corrosive medium from the outer layer, and will not penetrate the outer layer.
Outer layer (reinforcing layer): The required strength layer, made of non-woven cloth, short fiber felt.
Outermost layer: Its composition and structure are the same as the inner layer, and its purpose is to prevent the reinforcing layer from being exposed to the corrosive environment.

sections.text: Composite resin and auxiliary materials

sections.caption: Table 3-4-54 Epoxy resin and auxiliary materials
rows: Epoxy resin: Epoxy resin is a substance containing two or more epoxy groups per molecule. It has good mechanical properties, good corrosion resistance, good adhesion, good water resistance, and good chemical resistance. Epoxy resins are commonly used in the following types: ① Bisphenol A epoxy resin (general purpose epoxy resin): Its epoxy equivalent is about 190, with designation E-51, E-44, E-42, E-20, E-12. This type of resin has good usability, can be used with various curing agents, and can improve performance. ② Novolac epoxy resin: It has higher epoxy content and better corrosion resistance. This type of resin has good heat resistance, good corrosion resistance, and is commonly used in high-temperature corrosion-resistant glass fiber reinforced plastic. ③ Aliphatic epoxy resin: It is derived from aliphatic epoxides and has a lower epoxy equivalent, designated H-122, H-71, W-95, etc. This type of resin has good physical and mechanical properties, good heat resistance, and good weather resistance.

Curing agent: Curing agents can promote the cross-linking reaction of epoxy resins. Curing agents are generally divided into two categories: ① Amine curing agents: They are epoxy resins used for room temperature curing, including aliphatic amines, cycloaliphatic amines, aromatic amines, etc. Commonly used are diethylenetriamine (DETA), triethylenetetramine (TETA), tetraethylenepentamine (TEPA), and aliphatic amines, alicyclic amines, etc. ② Anhydride curing agents: They are used for high-temperature curing of epoxy resins. Commonly used are methylhexahydrophthalic anhydride (MHPA), hexahydrophthalic anhydride (HHPA), methyltetrahydrophthalic anhydride (MTHPA), and dodecanedioic anhydride (DDS), 4,4-diaminodiphenylmethane (MDA). Modifier: It can improve the brittleness of cured epoxy resin, improve toughness, improve adhesion, and improve processing performance. Commonly used modifiers include 590 type, 591 type, 593 type, and 120 type. Accelerator: It can accelerate the curing reaction. In addition to the accelerator, the epoxy resin curing system also uses many types of curing accelerators. It is necessary to select the appropriate temperature for curing. When heating, add a small amount of accelerator. 1.3 Degree of Freedom Analysis of Mechanisms

When designing a new mechanism structure, first identify all existing mechanisms, determine which are main components, and whether the mechanism can achieve definite motion. Therefore, first analyze the degree of freedom of the mechanism. To determine whether the mechanism can achieve definite motion, the degree of freedom F must satisfy: ① F > 0; ② The number of degrees of freedom equals the number of active components of the mechanism. If F = 0, the mechanism cannot move; if F > 0 and the number of active components is not equal to F, the mechanism cannot achieve predetermined motion. Conforming to these conditions, but due to structural dimensions being equal to the motion radius configuration, it can also achieve predetermined motion.

sections.text: 2 Kinematic Analysis of Planar Mechanisms

The kinematic analysis of mechanisms is based on the constraints imposed by the mechanism on the motion of its members. The main content of kinematic analysis includes: ① determining the position of each member in the mechanism; ② determining the velocity and acceleration of each point on the members; ③ determining the angular velocity and angular acceleration of each member.
Analysis methods: ① determine the motion characteristics and motion synthesis of the mechanism; ② serve as the basis for force analysis calculations.
Several kinematic analysis methods are compared in Table 4-1-10.

1.4 Structural analysis of planar mechanisms

Mechanism structural analysis is a method of design based on the mechanism motion diagram, conducting degree of freedom calculation, studying the mechanism structure type, and using this to conduct mechanism classification, so as to facilitate the classification of mechanism types and provide a general method for the kinematic and dynamic analysis of mechanism motion. The structural composition of planar mechanisms is shown in Table 4-1-9.

The basic structural elements of planar mechanisms are: a high pair and a low pair. A high pair is a pair of elements in contact at a point or along a curve in the mechanism, with two curved surfaces in contact at the curve center or at two points of tangency (point contact) or (arc contact) with rod connection. Using this low pair to replace a high pair. Except for points, straight lines, and circles as high pair elements, other curves have high pair elements that are not in contact with the contact point at the curve rate is variable, so the low pair of the same mechanism is different in different positions of the representative mechanism, so only the low pair mechanism in a certain position can receive the motion received.

3.3 Force Analysis of Mechanisms

The method commonly used in engineering is the graphical method of force analysis. It applies the principle of force balance to the relative structure on the machine, uses the equilibrium conditions of forces to find the forces required by the motion pair, and calls it static force analysis. For low-speed mechanisms with small moving mass, it is not necessary to consider inertial force; generally, for mechanisms with high-speed operation, inertial force must be considered. For mechanisms with rotating pairs at fixed positions, force analysis should be performed, and the applied friction torque (for rotating pairs) and friction force (for sliding pairs) should be included in the force diagram.

3.4.2 Balance of Planar Mechanisms

In planar mechanisms, there are inertia forces during the working cycle of the mechanism. During high-speed operation, the inertia forces and inertia moments generated by the moving parts are much larger than the working forces, and the changes in direction and magnitude of the inertia forces cause the mechanism to vibrate. The balance of the mechanism is to use the inertia forces acting on the lower part of the mechanism as vibration forces, which produces vibration.

3.4 Inertial force balance

To eliminate the small unbalanced inertial force on the attached additional mass and friction, the inertial force balance calculation should be performed to eliminate the unbalance caused by structural defects (such as structural asymmetry). Perform the balance sequence in the balance machine. For the balance of inertial forces, refer to the data in Table 8 and Table 8. For a given mechanism, the balance is called dynamic balance if the unbalanced inertial force is less than the specified value; otherwise it is called static balance. The balance must consider the vibration characteristics of the structure. The vibration mode is divided into 1, 2, 3, ... types according to the vibration mode quantity. The main factor affecting the vibration mode is the working speed range within the structure. When the vibration mode is low, the vibration mode is clearly distinguished; when the vibration mode is high, the vibration mode is more obvious. Therefore, according to the working requirements, the vibration mode should have its own vibration mode separation to ensure accuracy. Before performing the balance of the working member, generally the working member's natural frequency should be determined first, and then under certain conditions, the balance of the working member should be performed. This manual discusses the balance of the working member.

Rigid rotor balance: static balance (length ratio b/d < 0.2, high-speed use) is the basis for balance unbalanced inertial force; dynamic balance (length ratio large, high-speed use) is the basis for balance unbalanced inertial force and moment.

In vertical planar mechanism motion, the effect of the engine on the dynamic imbalance of the crank is manifested as vibration force. The vibration force and the motion of the connecting rod are completely lost in the precision measures of the mechanism's complete balance; and the imbalance of the connecting rod is the imbalance of the mechanism (incomplete balance). The method of balancing the planar mechanism is: ① when the mechanism has no crank simultaneous with the work, these structural management measures can make the vibration force reach complete balance; ② add a counterweight to the crank to balance the quality and distribution of the connecting rod (Table 4-1-25); ③ add a balance weight to the crank (Table 4-1-25). The method of adding counterweight is generally based on the principle of single weight addition, and after the counterweight is added, the mechanism's center of gravity position changes. In the 20th and 70th centuries, many methods were used to achieve complete balance of vibration force, and the method of adding vibration force to achieve complete balance was emphasized. To achieve complete balance of vibration force, it is necessary to use the fixed method, so that the structure can achieve the vibration force of the complete balance of the mechanism, and the single degree of freedom of the crank in the fixed road management of the mechanism is to achieve the vibration force of the complete balance of the mechanism. The vibration force imbalance of the crank is complex, requiring high structural requirements for vibration force balance. The vibration force balance of the mechanism will enable the mechanism to achieve complete balance of vibration force. In the 20th to 80th centuries, the vibration force imbalance of the mechanism and the vibration force of the mechanism were the smallest factors in the chemical balance of the standard comprehensive chemical balance, avoiding vibration; in the 90th century, the use of variable structural quality and distribution information and the imbalance of the balance weight and the complete balance of the vibration force and the vibration force imbalance of the 30 kinds of body structure.
The vibration force M is the standard measure of the imbalance, which is expressed as:
M_r = - (d/dt) Σ(i=1 to n) m_i(x_i*ÿ_i - y_i*ẍ_i + k_i*φ̈_i)

In the formula, x_i, y_i, ẍ_i, ÿ_i respectively represent the position and velocity values of the center of mass of component i in the fixed coordinate system; m_i, k_i are the mass and moment of inertia of component i; ω_i = J_ω/m_i; φ̈_i is the angular acceleration of component i; m is the number of active components.

To achieve complete balance of the vibration force of the mechanism, it is also necessary to achieve the combined balance of M_r = 0. Taking a four-bar mechanism as an example, if it has already achieved vibration force balance, the vibration force of the mechanism can be expressed as:

In the formula, a_i, r_i are respectively the crank length and distance from the center of rotation of the connecting rod; θ_i = (r⃗_i, a⃗_i) is the angle between the crank radius r⃗_i and the component mass a⃗_i (Figure 4-1-9); φ_i, φ̇_i, φ̈_i respectively represent the crank position, angular velocity, and angular acceleration.

sections.text: When the above conditions are satisfied, it is necessary to achieve the vibration force balance of the mechanism by adding a balance weight to the fixed frame 4 or point D.

To achieve planar mechanism balance, it is generally necessary to first design the mechanism structure to achieve management objectives, second to achieve vibration force balance, and third to add inertial balance weight to achieve complete balance of vibration force or partial balance.

The instantaneous center of the mechanism: each component has an instantaneous center. If a mechanism has N components, excluding the fixed frame, the mechanism has K = N(N-1)/2 instantaneous centers. The position of the instantaneous center: two components rotate and move together. At the same time, the instantaneous center is located on the line connecting the motion center and the guide line of the two components. When the two components move in a plane, the instantaneous center is at the intersection of the perpendiculars to the velocity directions of the two components.

Three-center theorem: if three components move relative to each other, their three instantaneous centers must be located on the same straight line. For example, in Figure 4-1-18, components 1, 2, and 4 have three instantaneous centers A, B, P₂₄ located on a straight line.

Using the instantaneous center to find the relative angular velocity of components: the relative angular velocity of the upper point of the component is equal to the relative angular velocity of the lower point or the absolute angular velocity (or absolute instantaneous center) divided by the distance from the point to the instantaneous center (or absolute instantaneous center).

sections.text: 4 Force Analysis of Mechanisms with One Degree of Freedom

The force analysis of mechanisms with one degree of freedom is based on understanding the following: ① determine the force transmitted by the mechanism; ② determine the force distribution on the mechanism; ③ determine the speed of the mechanism.
4.1 Motion Process and Motion Equation of Mechanisms

The two motions of a mechanism (usually represented by the main shaft) can be divided into two stages, as shown in Figure 4-1-10. In the starting stage, the mechanism has a certain acceleration at the beginning, and its characteristics are determined by the driving force applied to the mechanism, which allows the driving component to overcome the resistance, thus the mechanism responds with fine consideration of its motion characteristics and the corresponding settings are made.

In the constant speed stage, the main shaft speed of the mechanism is constant, that is, the motion is uniform. As shown in Figure 4-1-10 in the curve 1, (such as electric motors, etc.), or in the normal working speed corresponding to the average value ωm of the working cycle (period is t₁), the motion changes, that is, the speed motion, as shown in curve 2 in Figure 4-1-10 (such as certain reciprocating or rotary machine tools). This is the constant speed working stage of the mechanism, and its motion characteristics meet the requirements of the working machinery.
In the stopping stage, in order to shorten the parking time, the mechanism is equipped with a braking device.
The functional relationship of the mechanism in the motion process can be expressed by the following motion equation:
Ac - Ar - Af ± Ac = E₂ - E₁ (4-1-8)

sections.text: 4.2 Solution of Mechanism Motion Equations

In solving the motion equation to determine the force distribution and force analysis of the mechanism motion problem, the mechanism can be simplified into a two-body system connected by a shaft (rotational or translational) with a two-body structure. For this purpose, it is necessary to: ① replace all forces acting on the original mechanism with the driving force applied to the main shaft at the rotation point of the main shaft Fₘ (or driving torque Mₘ); ② replace the mass distribution of the original mechanism with the equivalent mass mₑq (or equivalent rotational inertia Jₑq) at the rotation point of the main shaft. After the mechanism is simplified, the motion equation can be solved, and the calculation formula is shown in 4-1-26. The application examples of the motion equation are shown in 4-1-27.
4.3 Adjustment and Design of Periodic Speed Fluctuation of Mechanism

The periodic speed fluctuation of a mechanism can be adjusted by automatically adjusting the driving force to maintain stable operation. When the mechanism completes one working cycle, the input and output energy (work) are equal, and the output is at a certain time interval, which will cause periodic speed fluctuation. For this reason, a flywheel must be installed in a working cycle to input or output energy that can have large periodic changes. The flywheel absorbs energy when the input is greater than the output, and releases energy when the output is greater than the input, thereby reducing the periodic speed fluctuation caused by the flywheel inertia. sections.text: Chapter 2 Design of Basic Mechanisms
1 Planar Linkage Mechanisms
1.1 Structural Types of Four-Bar Mechanisms

In planar linkage mechanisms, the most commonly used four-bar mechanism is applied. Only when certain special requirements are met should multi-bar mechanisms be used, or when the transmission characteristics and motion requirements are fixed, such as the center distance and rotation angle of the fixed pivot on the two sides of the first degree of freedom or the number of teeth and speed ratio of the fixed gear pair, etc.

The most basic four-bar mechanism is a four-bar linkage with four moving pairs. Figure 4-2-1 shows a mechanism where member 4 is the machine, members 1, 3 and the frame are connected, called the frame. Its member 1 is relative to the machine frame and can rotate continuously, called the crank. Member 3 is relative to the machine frame at a certain angle, called the rocker. Member 2 is the connecting rod between the crank and rocker, called the connecting rod. This type of mechanism is called a four-bar linkage mechanism, which is the most common type of linkage mechanism.

The linkage mechanism, compared with the gear linkage, has the selection of the connecting rod as the condition for the linkage of the crank: (1) The minimum bar length + the maximum bar length ≤ the sum of the other two bar lengths; (2) The frame length - the selected bar length ≤ the other connecting rod length ≤ the frame length + the selected bar length. The structural types of common four-bar mechanisms are shown in Table 4-1-16.

4.3.1 Mean Angular Velocity ωm of Machine Main Shaft and Speed Non-Uniformity Coefficient δ
The mean angular velocity ωm of the main shaft is expressed in two ways:
(1) Arithmetic mean (commonly used in engineering)
ωm = (ωmax + ωmin) / 2
Where ωmax, ωmin are the maximum and minimum angular velocity values in one operating cycle.
(2) Actual mean value
Instantaneous angular velocity ω as a function of rotation angle φ:
ωm = (1/φ) ∫₀^φ ω(φ) dφ
Instantaneous angular velocity ω as a function of time t:
ωm = (1/t) ∫₀^t ω(t) dt
Speed non-uniformity coefficient δ:
δ = (ωmax - ωmin) / ωm

Where δ represents the coefficient of angular velocity variation within one operating cycle. δ is small, the machine's speed fluctuation is small. Various types of machines have different allowable speed non-uniformity coefficients δᵢ (refer to Table 4-1-28). The design of flywheels should meet δ≤δ₀.

Selection principle of δ: ① Ensure work quality; ② Do not exceed δ₀ to avoid large wheel diameter and economic loss; ③ When using electric motor drive, consider the motor's speed regulation characteristics. The maximum, minimum angular velocities ωmax, ωmin, mean angular velocity ωm, and speed non-uniformity coefficient δ are in the following relationship:
ωmax = ωm(1 + δ/2)
ωmin = ωm(1 - δ/2)
ωmax² - ωmin² = 2δωm²

Machine design is based on the complete operation of one cycle. Its task is to simulate the machine's motion, can change the situation (use large diameter A₁ or can increase ΔE as shown), the machine's required speed non-uniformity coefficient δ and flywheel shaft speed nf, to determine the flywheel's rotational inertia Jf, from the specified flywheel size.

The transmission angle of the four-bar linkage is the angle between the connecting rod and the output crank at the instant of transmission (Figure 4-2-2). sections.text: 4.4 Calculation of Mechanical Efficiency
Mechanical efficiency η is a quantitative indicator of the ability of a machine to utilize the input power.
η = Pₑ/Pₛ = 1 - Pₘ/Pₛ = Pₛ/(Pₛ + Pₘ) (4-1-18)

The torque required to overcome the load torque Jl can be obtained by using the auxiliary hand machinery system dynamics analysis, that is, using the substitution method Jdn = J0 + Jl. Substitute into formulas (6) or (8) in Table 4-1-26, find ωmax, ωmin, δ = (ωmax - ωmin)/ωn. Verify that the condition δ ≤ δp is satisfied. If not, increase Jl (Jl is the flywheel moment of inertia), then recalculate until δ ≤ δp. The Jl obtained is the flywheel moment of inertia required. This method has high precision and strong applicability. In engineering practice, this method is often used.

The flywheel torque fluctuation is determined by the maximum torque reaching the structural position on the driving force distance Mdrag, blocking force distance Mblock, and the motor output torque distance Mmotor. The difference between the maximum driving force and blocking force is Ad. The calculation method for Ad has multiple forms, which can be seen in Table 4-1-27 to Table 4-1-30. Then calculate Jl = (Ad/δp²) - J0, so Jl = (91.194/δp²) - J0. Calculate the flywheel moment of inertia Jl. sections.text: 1.3 Design of Four-Bar Mechanism with Input and Output Shaft Position Constraints

The position relationship design of input and output shafts and connecting rods can use geometric methods, analytical methods, or graphical-analytical methods. Geometric methods are relatively simple and are often used in general design, but they only require that the input and output shafts have no definite position relationship, and the analysis method is not precise enough; the analytical method can be used within a certain range to determine the motion law, with high precision, and can eliminate the error between the design requirements and the actual motion (the four-bar mechanism cannot completely meet the design requirements), but the calculation is cumbersome; experiments are the most reliable method to select the basic dimensions of the mechanism, with high precision and low cost for similar design and structural size selection.

1.4.6 Congruent Mechanisms and Their Applications

In mechanism design, it is sometimes possible to realize the design where the connecting rod of the selected mechanism can achieve the desired motion, but the fixed pivot and moving pivot cannot be easily placed in the mechanism, or the transmission angle is not suitable. When encountering such problems, the principle of congruent mechanisms can be used to use another pair of non-congruent mechanisms to solve the problem. The congruent mechanism diagram is as follows (Figure 4-2-27):

The horizontal quadrilateral DCPC', forming triangle PC'H and BCP similar, KH'C'D is the mechanism ABCD of another congruent mechanism, P point is the connecting rod C'H above the point.

2.2.2 Eccentric Circular Gears and Non-Circular Gear Shafts

For a pair of gears, the pressure angle and the center distance are equal to the corresponding eccentric circular gears, which can use similar substitution methods to achieve similar regular changes in output speed. This gear transmission is simple and economical. It has two calculation methods: (1) The minimum center distance is the standard center distance, the rotation center is slightly offset from the standard center distance, and the two gears use standard gears; use the new eccentric center distance to ensure continuous transmission, so the calculation should be combined. (2) Take the driving center distance greater than the standard center distance, as the standard center distance, to avoid transmission through the center distance being too small.

sections.text: 3 Cam Mechanism Structure
The cam mechanism is a high-pair mechanism formed by the motion of the driven member during the working period. Its main advantages are as follows.

Advantages: (1) The motion law of the driven member can be arbitrarily specified, and the cam mechanism can be used for both the motion law that requires the driven member to move according to a specified trajectory, and also for the motion law that requires the driven member to move according to a specified time function. The motion time and the follower motion law can both be arbitrarily specified. It can achieve high-speed motion, and the motion can be smooth. (2) The structure is compact, the mechanism is simple, and the calculation is relatively simple. In particular, it is easy to implement with computer-aided design and control, making the cam mechanism more suitable for automation.

Disadvantages: (1) At the high-pair contact point, it is difficult to ensure good lubrication. Due to the high contact pressure, it is easy to cause wear. To maintain the required service life, the transmission force cannot be too large. (2) In high-speed cam mechanisms, the motion characteristics of the high-pair contact are relatively complex, and precise analysis and design are more difficult.

sections.text: 3.3 Pressure Angle of Spur Gears

The pressure angle is related to whether the spur gear structure can transmit motion smoothly when receiving force. Whether the pressure angle is large or small determines the base pitch of the spur gear. If the pressure angle is large, the base pitch can be small, so the spur gear size is small; conversely, if the pressure angle is small, the base pitch is large, and the spur gear size is large. When the pressure angle exceeds a certain limit value, the gear will self-lock. In design, when the base pitch is required to have a certain value, the base pitch can be increased to reduce the pressure angle, so that the gear can work well; conversely, if a smaller pressure angle is required, the base pitch must be reduced accordingly. When the pressure angle is too small, the base pitch becomes too large, which may exceed the installation space. The pressure angle of the spur gear is determined by the base pitch diameter and the small pitch diameter. When the base pitch diameter is constant, the pressure angle increases with the increase of the small pitch diameter. When the pressure angle exceeds a certain limit value, the gear will self-lock. In the calculation, when the base pitch is required to have a certain value, the base pitch can be increased to reduce the pressure angle. For the structure of spur gears, the pressure angle also changes with the change of the spur gear angle (the change of the involute profile during the meshing process). 3.5.1 Motion Rules of Driven Members

Vm, Am, Jm respectively represent the maximum velocity, maximum acceleration, and maximum jerk in the motion rule. Table 4-2-21 shows the characteristic values of various motion rules. Generally, the motion rule is selected based on the dynamic characteristics that change with speed. The current commonly used motion rules are grouped into motion rules. It is required that Vm, Am, Jm, and (ΔV)m are all minimum values. If the motion rule is not set, it should be selected according to the working conditions.

1) High-speed light load: Each characteristic value itself is large. Am, Vm, Jm, (ΔV)m should be considered. Am should be small. When the driven member has a large load, the contact stress is large, and the relationship between the dynamic force and the motion rule should be considered. Generally, the high contact stress should be selected to reduce the Am rule. Improving the motion rule of Am is a lighter design of the motion rule.

2) Medium speed: Each characteristic value itself is large, (ΔV)m, Jm should be considered. Vm is large, the motion is large, the bearing capacity and power transmission efficiency are large. For small load driven members, the noise is large. Vm has a large impact on the wheel size and speed. When the wheel size is small, Vm is large, the maximum force is large (except for equal motion), conversely, the same Vm, the wheel size is small, improving the equal motion rule is relatively ideal.

3) Low-speed heavy load: It requires Am, Vm, Jm, (ΔV)m and other characteristic values to be small. sections.text: Solution: Divide the motion region as follows:

1. In 0° ≤ θ < 40°: from the motion law "rise, dwell, fall", consider the relative speed of the rise phase, and the corresponding rise motion angle is 2 × 40° = 80°. Refer to the equal rise-equal dwell-equal fall motion equation, then:
s₁ = 4h₁(θ/80°)²
s₁'(θ) = 8h₁(θ/80°) × (180°/(80° × π)) = (18h₁/π)(θ/80°)
When θ = 40°: (s₁')_{θ=40°} = 9h/π

2. In 40° ≤ θ ≤ 70°: the speed is constant; at point A (θ = 40°) the two motion laws have equal speed, then:
s₂'(θ) = (s₁'(θ))_{θ=40°} = 9h/π
Set point A's displacement as s₂, then:
s₂ = h₁(θ - 40°) × (9/180°) = (h/20)(θ - 40°)
When θ = 70°: s₂ = 3h₁/2

3. In 70° ≤ θ ≤ 130°: from the motion law "rise, dwell, fall", consider the relative deceleration phase, the relative motion angle starts from θ₀ = 10° and the relative motion region is 120°. Refer to the equal rise-equal dwell-equal fall motion equation, with point B as the starting point, the displacement equation is:
s₃ = 2h₃[1-2((θ-10°)/120°)²] (h₃ only deceleration)
s₃'(θ) = (12/π)h₁((130°-θ)/120°)

The involute spur gear working surface divides the tooth into non-working surface and working surface. The normal machine control method is used to draw the tooth profile. The tooth profile design must satisfy the following three basic conditions:

items: The common tangent point of the two tooth surfaces must be on the line of action, and the tooth profile contact point must satisfy the basic condition of the involute gear.

4 Indexing Cam Mechanism
4.1 Performance and Motion Parameters of Indexing Cam Mechanism

In an indexing cam mechanism, the main component is a cam, which is generally a plate cam connected to a rotating shaft. It is driven by a motor with multiple teeth on the shaft, and can be designed according to the working requirements for intermittent motion. This type of mechanism does not require other auxiliary devices to complete the required precision positioning. Table 4.2-44 lists several commonly used time-sharing indexing mechanisms.

The indexing cam mechanism generally works at high speed, and in the working process, in order to select the motion law that best meets the requirements, the main consideration is the dynamic characteristics of the mechanism. Generally, the hope is that the motion transfer occurs at the beginning and end of the indexing period with an angular velocity ω. The angular velocity ω₂ is equal to zero. During the indexing period, the angular velocity and angular acceleration change continuously without sudden changes. The lower the inertia, the better the use of high-speed indexing and angular acceleration maximum value ωmax and a₂max, the smaller the motion mechanism. 4.3 Circular Column Eccentric Circular Gear Mechanism
4.3.1 Working Principle and Main Types

Figure 4-2.66a shows a circular column eccentric circular gear mechanism. The driving gear 1 is circular, and the driven gear 2 is equipped with several small circular gears arranged radially around it. When the driving gear rotates, its eccentric center drives the driven gear to rotate eccentrically. When the driven gear reaches the lowest point, the two non-meshing teeth are locked by the circular column on the housing to prevent the driven gear from rotating. When the driven gear reaches the highest point, the teeth on the driven gear are released from the locking position. The circular column teeth on the housing are arranged in the same eccentric manner as the driving gear, making it easy to achieve high reduction ratios. The circular column eccentric circular gear mechanism has the advantages of simple structure, low speed in the middle section, easy combination, and the ability to achieve multiple-stage eccentric circular gear reduction in a single housing. It can achieve higher reduction ratios with fewer stages, making it suitable for applications requiring high reduction ratios and low speed.

5.2 Friction Wheel Mechanism
5.2.1 Working Principle and Form

The friction wheel mechanism (also called friction drive mechanism) can convert the motion direction of the driving wheel into a rotational motion around the driven shaft for single-cycle periodic motion. Commonly used in various positioning mechanisms. The basic form of the friction wheel mechanism is divided into external friction (Figure 4-2-77), internal friction (Table 4-2-69 Figure b) and spherical friction wheel mechanism (Table 4-2-72) three types. The external friction wheel mechanism is mainly used for intermittent rotation, and the friction wheel stops when the driving wheel rotates. The internal friction wheel mechanism is opposite. The rotation time of the spherical friction wheel mechanism is equal to the stop time.

sections.text: 4.4 Common (Parallel) Degree Cycloidal Gear Mechanism
4.4.1 Basic Structure and Working Principle

The common degree cycloidal gear mechanism uses two shafts parallel to the main shaft to transmit motion. The driving gear 1 is located in front (or below), and the two driven gears are composed of the front and rear discs. When the driving gear rotates, the driven gears on the front and rear discs mesh with it respectively. The front and rear tooth surfaces of the driven gear mesh with the corresponding tooth surfaces of the driving gear. When the driven gear rotates, its front and rear tooth surfaces mesh with the corresponding tooth surfaces of the driving gear. The relative displacement of the tooth surfaces causes the driven gear to rotate. When the driven gear rotates, the front and rear tooth surfaces mesh with the corresponding tooth surfaces of the driving gear. The relative displacement of the tooth surfaces causes the driven gear to rotate. Due to the mechanical structure being two-stage cycloidal gears, the design requirements for the tooth profile and installation are relatively high.
(1) Single-head Type

The turntable rotates once per revolution, rotating one tooth circle angle. For example, as shown in Figure 4-2-69a, the head H = 1, the number of teeth z = 8, the tooth pitch angle φᵢ = 2πH/z - π/4. This type of mechanism has the characteristic that the tooth rotates half a circle per revolution.
(2) Multi-head Type

The turntable rotates once per revolution, rotating multiple tooth circle angles. Figure 4-2-69b shows H = 2, z = 8, φᵢ = π/2; Figure 4-2-69c shows H = 4, z = 4, φᵢ = 2π. The multi-head type mechanism has the characteristic that the tooth rotates one circle per revolution.

sections.text: 5.3 Incomplete Gear Wheel Mechanism

Incomplete gear wheel mechanism converts the continuous rotation of the driving gear into intermittent rotation of the driven gear. Its advantage is that it can limit the motion range of the driven gear mechanism, design flexibly, but must be selected from the driving gear at each intermittent operation start, without sudden impact, to generally be used for indexing, light load and intermittent impact on normal work combination. If no continuous load is applied, the mechanism can improve the dynamic performance.
5.3.1 Basic Form and Meshing Characteristics

Incomplete gear wheel mechanism is divided into two types: tooth and tooth gap (Figure 4-2-82, Figure 4-2-83). The mechanism consists of three parts: main wheel 1 and driving wheel 2; a pair of locking teeth 3, the driving tooth on the main wheel can directly cut into or be equipped with, can also be composed of a pair of locking teeth; the elastic or sliding return mechanism starts, the design of the mechanism improves the dynamic performance. This article only discusses the elastic structure and dynamic analysis and design.

Meshing characteristics of incomplete gear wheels: each intermittent operation can be completed by one pair of tooth engagement, can also be completed by several pairs of tooth engagement, incomplete gear wheel mechanism first, no pair of tooth engagement with incomplete gear wheel mechanism.

First tooth: from the driving wheel's stop position, should be at the self-locking position of the main wheel, the first tooth can be guided through the two fixed points G, with the driving wheel's locking tooth engagement (Figure 4-2-84a, b). Starting point E from the driving wheel's stop position F determines, it can be at the main wheel's top tooth on the line GB (Figure b) or the tooth line B₁P⊥ (Figure a). sections.text: 3 Gear-Rod Combined Mechanism

Gear-rod combined mechanisms can achieve various types of motion requirements, but the bearing capacity and processing requirements are balanced. Therefore, under certain conditions, using gear-rod combined mechanisms can also achieve the required motion requirements, which is a design compromise. This type of combined mechanism has gear mechanisms, and many use cycloidal gear systems.
3.1 Planetary Gear System and II-level Rod Combined Mechanism

This type of combined mechanism consists of a planetary gear mechanism that combines external and internal gears with a II-level rod mechanism. Generally, the planetary gear's rotation is active, and the planetary gear is used as the driving element, so that the output member achieves complex motion.
(1) Single External Mesh Planetary Gear System and Slider Rod Combined Mechanism

This type of combined mechanism is as shown in Figure 4-3-12. Point C on the external line curve changes the external line curve width. When k = 1/3, point C₂'s trajectory is a straight line that does not pass through the center. As shown in Figure 3, when point C is at the position of the straight line, the output rod 4 will produce near-linear motion. sections.text: 4 Cam-gear combined mechanisms

Cam-gear combined mechanisms are composed of various types of cam mechanisms (including shaft cams, plate cams, cylindrical cams, etc.) and gear mechanisms. This type of combined mechanism generally uses gear mechanisms as the main body, cam mechanisms for control and adjustment, and supplements the work of gears to achieve the special motion requirements of pure gear mechanisms.
4.1 Output shaft realizing periodic variable speed motion of cam-gear combined mechanisms

Figure 4-3-27 shows a cam-gear mechanism and a columnar gear mechanism combined mechanism. It uses a non-conjugate gear mechanism in the gear train of the packaging machine, where the main drive is a columnar gear 1. When the input shaft ω₁ is rotated by an angle, the columnar gear 1 continuously rotates the spur gear, and the spur gear rotates at the same time as the shaft ω₁. The motion of the spur gear is controlled by the cam, so the spur gear rotates at a constant angular velocity, and the design steps and methods are as follows.
① The spur gear 1' does not rotate with the shaft ω₁, and the worm's angular velocity is ω₂'.
ω₂' = ω₁z₁/z₂
Where z₁ — the number of teeth on the worm gear; z₂ — the number of teeth on the worm.
② The spur gear 1' does not rotate with the shaft, and the gear's angular velocity is ω₂'.

For example, when the input shaft rotates, the point M on the driving link moves with speed mm', and the work machine 6 is driven by the composite linkage mechanism (Figure 4-3-23). When the driving gear 10 rotates continuously, the M point motion speed is mm', and the work machine 6 is driven by the composite linkage mechanism. The relative position of point M's motion speed and the relative position of gears m'm' and m'm' can be changed by adjusting point M's motion speed relative to the gear teeth pattern, to meet the non-return requirements of the work machine. 4.3 Output Implementation of Periodic Dwell of Fixed Gear-Spur Gear Combined Mechanism

Figure 4-3-30 shows a combined mechanism composed of a cycloidal gear system and a fixed spur gear. The cycloidal gear system has a driving gear H as the main component. The output gear in the center is gear 1, and it shares the common axis O₁ with the driving gear H. When the driving gear H rotates one cycle, the fixed gear 3 undergoes curved slot motion. When the driving gear H rotates at an angular velocity ω, the continuous rotation of the output spur gear can achieve periodic dwell motion in a specific angular range. In this combined mechanism, the spur gear can control the motion of the output gear. For the design of this fixed spur gear-cycloidal gear combined mechanism, the design principle and method are as follows.

This type of reciprocating quadrilateral mechanism has a transmission ratio equal to 1, and the instantaneous transmission ratio is:
i₃₁ = ω₃/ω₁ = AP/DP = (b² - a²)/((b² + c²) + 2abcosφ₁)

When φ₁ = 0°, i₃₁ = (i₃₁)ₘₐₓ = -(b+a)/(b-a)

When the main crank rotates at a uniform angular velocity, the driven crank undergoes non-uniform motion. This forms an unstable state of the mechanism during operation. When the crank continues to rotate forward, the driven crank can rotate with the main crank at the same time. To avoid this, special devices (such as point guides) or follower guides must be used to pass through the mechanism's unstable state.

F = QL₂/(L₁cosα)

In the formula, α is the angle between rod 3, 4 and ED line; L₁, L₂ are the distances from the force F and P to the pivot axis L of the vertical distance. 2 Degrees of Freedom Analysis of Mechanical Components—Design Principles to Meet Motion Requirements

The basic nature of machinery is constrained motion. Therefore, it must satisfy the design principles required for motion. The commonly used method for analyzing the degrees of freedom of mechanical components is related to the "mechanism principle" in the course, but there are significant differences.
2.1 Degrees of Freedom of Mechanical Components

A mechanical component in space has six degrees of freedom, namely movements and rotations along and around the X, Y, Z three axes. As shown in Figure 5-1-1, these six degrees of freedom can be represented using the coordinate system shown in Figure 5-1-1b. The three axes of the coordinate system represent the movement directions, and the unmarked axes represent the movement directions that cannot be moved. sections.text: 2.3 Application of Degree of Freedom Analysis in Connection Design

The connection definition stipulates that one part A and another part B (or base) are fixed together, so there is no relative motion. Figure 5-1-2 shows part A with six degrees of freedom. If part A is fixed on part B, it can be understood as removing the constraints required to eliminate the six degrees of freedom of A.

The combined form of the connection is mainly seen in two types: one is a flat surface (Figure 5-1-2a). When using bolts, rivets, welding and other methods to connect, most parts belong to this type; the other is a cylindrical surface connection (Figure 5-1-2b). When using pins, bolts, disc couplings and other forms of connection, most parts belong to this type. In the plane connection, the main role is to eliminate the degrees of freedom in the plane. The flat surface connection table 5-1-2 shows 5 types of structures, which can eliminate two degrees of freedom (note that these degrees of freedom are removed by half), and then eliminate the remaining degrees of freedom, and perform the necessary strength calculation.

1 Content, Requirements, and Basic Conditions of Mechanical Structure Design

sections.caption: Table 5-1-1
