In the mechanical design process, after the design scheme is determined and before the mechanical structure design is carried out, the task is to follow the correct design principles, select appropriate structural design, and serve as the carrier of the machine. The mechanical structure design content should clarify the structure and relative relationships of the machine, determine the geometric shape, size, material, surface treatment method, heat treatment and other aspects.
1) The machine must have the required functions. The designed mechanism must have the functions required by users, such as achieving the required process operations, running smoothly, and the machine's own friction resistance.
2) The machine should have reliable performance. The mechanical parts should have sufficient strength, rigidity, wear resistance, corrosion resistance, and other properties that can meet the requirements.
3) Meet the requirements of the machine. Such as noise, use safety, reliability, etc.
4) Meet the requirements of the process. Such as material selection, mechanical processing, heat treatment, inspection, assembly, transportation, installation, debugging, use and management, and easy disassembly and maintenance.
5) Prevent corrosion, avoid dust and debris. Including saving raw materials, reducing processing of parts in harsh environments, reducing waste and extending service life. Reduce environmental pollution during use.
6) Economy. Strive to use the combined economy well, and be able to achieve economic benefits.

1) The design of the mechanical system should have all the functions and each sub-function required by it. The main functions include: production capacity, pressure, speed, displacement, etc.
2) Input and output of the system. Material requirements such as bed, information transmission, signal requirements, such as bed accuracy, information accuracy, signal accuracy, etc.
3) The basic requirements of the machine itself. Such as size, weight, noise, vibration, etc.

2) Material properties. Power, fuel, raw materials, lubricants, and other material supply conditions.
3) Operating conditions of the machine. Technical level and operating skills of operators, maintenance level, and technical requirements for operation and maintenance.
4) Economic conditions of use. Cost, maintenance, protection, material and equipment opening and closing effects on the machine's economic benefits.
5) Safety conditions. Personal safety and safety requirements, safety and safety (instructions) of operators.
6) Use characteristics of the machine. Such as certain national standards for color, design, and special requirements.

1) Consider the production location of the product in the production process, add technical and equipment requirements, large-scale, high-precision equipment information, key process technology, new technology, new process, and related technical requirements.

1) Whether the market has similar products, whether the design is reasonable or not: design, production, sales, and whether there are competitive advantages?

3) Whether the market demand and current market situation of the market, product sales and future development expectations.

sections.text: 3 Techniques for Mechanical Structure Scheme Design

The main points for mechanical structure scheme design are two-fold: first, structural scheme design, which can be applied to multiple structural schemes for a given principle scheme; second, in order to use the design well, the design should fully consider multiple structural schemes for comparison. Second, determine the optimal scheme among these schemes. To improve design quality, the first stage requires outlining possible structural design schemes, and the second stage requires screening and analysis of various factors to select the optimal structural design scheme. This section describes how to expand thinking to control structural design schemes.

sections.text: Chapter 2 Design Principles for Improving Strength, Stiffness, and Extended Fatigue Life

Ensuring that mechanical parts have sufficient strength and stiffness is a basic requirement for mechanical design. Mechanical parts with insufficient strength will break or fracture, which will not affect the overall performance of the machine. If the strength is insufficient, the deformation will be large, which will affect the normal operation of the machine and reduce the service life of the machine. In recent years, it has become increasingly important to prevent the occurrence of fatigue failure and extend the fatigue life of machines. The implementation measures mainly include: (1) reducing the stress concentration of mechanical parts, (2) reducing the stress amplitude of mechanical parts, (3) improving the strength of mechanical materials, and (4) improving the surface quality of mechanical parts to reduce the safety factor.

sections.text: 2.6 Elastic strengthening and plastic strengthening principles

Before the component receives external load, the production process and external load direction are opposite to the elastic deformation caused by production, which is the elastic strengthening caused by the production process. After receiving external load, the pre-stress can offset part of the working stress of the component, called elastic strengthening. For example, Figure 5-2-8a shows the pre-stress of a shaft. The shaft uses high-strength material and special treatment to make the shaft produce pre-stress as shown in Figure 5-2-8b. When the beam acts as a two-way support with the same load, the stress under load is opposite to the pre-stress, and the pre-stress and working stress are mutually offset, achieving the most reasonable stress distribution as shown in Figure 5-2-8d. Plastic strengthening is the method of making the component produce plastic deformation, so that its yield strength is increased, and the part of the component that produces plastic deformation has a larger yield strength. Figure 5-2-9a shows the component before plastic deformation, Figure 5-2-9b shows the residual stress after plastic deformation. Figure 5-2-9c is the stress remaining after loading, and the stress in the component is added to the residual stress as shown in Figure 5-2-9d. The result is shown in Figure 5-2-9e, the final stress is less than the elastic strength limit, and the stress distribution can also adopt the plastic strengthening method to reduce its maximum stress ([§5-2-9i]).

sections.text: 5.3 Rational Layout Support Principles

Support conditions have a significant impact on the rigidity and strength of shaft components. For shaft components with different support conditions, the maximum bending moment M_max and maximum deflection f_max will have obvious differences. From this perspective, the rigidity and strength of the support structure are different. To improve the rigidity and strength of the support, the support point should be fixed by rigid connection to the shaft, and the support characteristics should be as close as possible to fixed support, thereby further improving the rigidity.

To improve the rigidity of flat castings, ribs are often needed. The rib height is approximately 0.8 times the wall thickness of the casting. Figure 5-2-28 shows several common rib application types. 3.3 Adoption of Surface Treatment to Improve Fatigue Strength Criterion

Using surface pressure, shot peening, carburizing and nitriding and other methods to strengthen the chemical composition of the surface, can improve the fatigue strength of components. It should be noted that the surface hardening layer cannot be interrupted. If interrupted, on the side, at the soft surface exchange place, the fatigue strength is significantly reduced. As shown in Figure 5-2-15, the tooth surface hardness is taken as an example. Its diagram (a) is incorrect, and diagram (b) is correct. If the entire tooth profile (including the tooth root, tooth root and full surface) is hardened and fire-treated, the fatigue strength can be improved to 1.85 times. If the work surface is quenched, due to soft surface exchange at the root, the fatigue strength reduction is about 80% of the original.

Example 1 A large-scale flying crane cable breaks directly, causing the steel wire rope to lose its function.

Figure 5-2-16 is a schematic diagram of a large flying crane transmission device. The electric motor drives a speed reducer, one end of which is connected to a steel wire rope, lifting a 1-ton load. The lifting height is 3 m. When lifting, the motor drives the reducer to rotate. The reducer's flying wheel rotates, and the motor continues to drive for 3-5 minutes. Then the electric motor reverses and the flying crane descends (reverse rotation). The load falls to the ground, completing a one-way cycle. According to the design calculation, the lifting force of the steel wire rope is F = 15 kN.

During the inspection of the steel wire rope, the following problems were found:
(1) At the opening of the outer steel wire rope surface, there are multiple broken wires. Within a distance of 10 roots, there are 10 broken wires. According to the "Lifting Machine Safety Management Regulations," the safety factor is 7 for personnel lifting devices with 6×19 steel wire rope. One broken wire distance surface fracture number exceeds 8 roots, which should be reported and the steel wire rope should be replaced.

4 Design Principles for Improving Contact Strength

Gears, bearings, sliding shaft bearings and other mechanical parts have working surfaces that are contact or friction surfaces. The force distribution should be distributed at different points, and the force should be distributed as much as possible. The design principles for improving contact strength are as follows.
4.1 Increase the Combined Radius of Curvature of the Contact Part

Figure 5-2-17 shows six types of groove structures. Figure a shows two mutually engaged groove contacts. The radius of curvature is small, and the contact strength is low. Figure b increases the radius of curvature of one contact surface. Compared to the radius of curvature of the other surface being unlimited, the contact strength is improved. Figure c and Figure d show that when using a flat surface method, the combined radius of curvature is further increased, and the contact force is reduced. Figure e shows that the radius of curvature of both surfaces is similar, so the contact stress is the smallest.
This method uses a line contact (linear contact) instead of a point contact (point contact), which is a common method to improve contact strength.

In Figure 5-2-17, the contact position uses the material provided by the material to improve the contact strength. To facilitate external installation, standard tapered rollers (GB/T 308-2002) can be used.

Chapter 3 Structural Design Principles for Improving Wear Resistance
1 Principle of Reducing Friction Surface Pressure
1.1 Methods for Reducing Friction Surface Pressure

(1) Increase the bearing surface area, the most commonly used method, but subject to the constraints of machine size and weight. (2) Use hydraulic pressure relief device. Figure 5-3-1 shows a pressure relief system and a pressure relief guide rail structure diagram. The guide rail is divided into two parts: the pressure relief part P and the guide part, where the pressure (static pressure) is applied. The pressure relief part is a single relief element with a load capacity F. Comparing the load capacity F with the bearing load F, that is, αₓ = F/F. The typical range is 0.4 ~ 0.7. To prevent the guide from shifting, αₓ should take a smaller value.

The cover layer serves to prevent light metal and corrosion-resistant alloy interface separation, thereby reducing or avoiding corrosion. The following requirements should be met for protective cover layers:

sections.text: During operation, impact and friction on the punch toward the punch proceed with wear. The punch has a certain amount of clearance. When the punch is subjected to oblique force, the gas in the punch cavity is compressed, causing the punch to use up its storage capacity. When the punch head is subjected to oblique impact, the gas in the punch has elastic rebound effect, strengthening the oblique impact force. This machine's deflection is the source of the punch force, so it cannot use elastic rebound equipment. When the sliding shaft is subjected to bending, it cannot meet the requirements. sections.text: (4) Improving the Impact Hardness of Punch Material

In the impact test on the punch, the impact hardness Ak (unit: J) is compared with the cross-sectional area (cm²) of the test specimen, called the impact hardness αk (unit: J/cm²). When the environmental temperature decreases, the material transitions from ductile to brittle state, and the impact hardness decreases significantly. To improve the impact hardness of the punch: reduce the content of carbon (C), phosphorus (P) and other impurities in the steel; use fine grains, use low-carbon martensite structure, use high-temperature tempering (austenite) structure. Remove internal defects in the steel (segregation, non-metallic inclusions, cracks, pores, etc.) to improve impact hardness, reduce cold brittleness transformation temperature, reduce cold brittleness transformation tendency; improve composite steel with Ni, Mn, Cu, Nb content, use fine grain, high-temperature tempered martensite (austenite) structure, require V, Ti content controlled within a certain range. Surface heat treatment (high temperature, medium temperature tempering) and chemical treatment (carburizing, nitriding) generally reduce impact hardness.
5 Structural Design Principles for Improving Rigidity
Factors affecting machine rigidity include: elastic modulus of component materials, component size and shape in the bearing surface, load-bearing capacity, etc.
5.1 Selecting Materials with High Elastic Modulus

Steel has the largest elastic modulus (carbon and alloy steel elastic modulus E = 206GPa), cast iron is slightly smaller, ball bearing steel and cast steel are even smaller. Copper alloys and aluminum alloys have elastic modulus about 1/3-1/2 of steel. Therefore, to meet the rigidity requirements of multi-steel components, in industrial applications of metal materials, steel has the highest elastic modulus. Only tungsten (W, elastic modulus E = 400GPa), molybdenum (Mo, elastic modulus E = 350GPa), beryllium (Be, elastic modulus E = 310GPa) have higher elastic modulus, but they are too expensive and difficult to use. These materials cannot provide the required rigidity for components. The choice of materials should focus on the most commonly used materials to improve dimensions and shapes to improve rigidity.
5.2 Principles of Tension, Compression Substitution for Bending

7 Principles for Selecting Appropriate Materials

To improve the precision of machinery, appropriate materials with stable dimensions should be selected, such as cast iron for flat plates, angles, and other precision components with high rigidity. Cast iron has good dimensional stability. After natural aging or artificial heat treatment, it should be completely stress-relieved, have minimal deformation, be easy to machine to small surface roughness, be corrosion-resistant, have no rust, have good surface finish after machining, have excellent damping characteristics, vibration resistance, and low cost. Its main disadvantage is brittleness. In recent years, both domestic and foreign countries have increasingly used cast iron as the basic component for precision machinery, such as the worktable of coordinate measuring machines, guide rails, guide screws, etc., which are not suitable for use with air-floating guide rails and working surfaces.

sections.text: Chapter 5 Principles for Structural Design to Improve Precision

To improve the precision of machine tool installation, in addition to improving the precision of each working part, attention should also be paid to adopting beneficial structural design for precision improvement. This can make each component have the same working precision as the machine tool installation, and the overall precision of the machine tool installation can be ensured. The following methods are commonly used.
1 Abbe (Abbe) Principle—Measured Dimension and Reading Dimension Coincident Line Principle

sections.caption: Table 5-5-1
rows: Abbe Principle: To ensure that the measuring instrument is installed on the same extension line as the measured result, the measuring instrument's reading scale must be located on the extension line of the measured dimension. In precision measurement instruments, this is the most important guiding principle.

The diagram shows a working platform guided by a guide rail system. Due to the guide rail's own error, the working platform will have lateral runout. The working platform's actual length is CD, and the measured length is AB. Since the measuring device is not on the extension line of the measured dimension, ED = Δl is the measurement error. Due to the Abbe principle, Δl = (l/Rb) = φh. This can be reduced by making h as small as possible to eliminate the impact of angular error. The prerequisite is that the Abbe principle requires h = 0.

sections.text: Chapter 4 Structural Design to Improve Corrosion Resistance

Improving the corrosion resistance of structures is mainly achieved through: selecting corrosion-resistant materials, adopting structures with good corrosion resistance, using slow corrosion and storage technologies, etc.
1 Common Classification of Corrosion
According to the causes of corrosion generation, it can be divided into the following four categories;

sections.caption: Table 5-4-1

There is friction or relative motion between the contact surfaces of the parts, causing corrosion of the corrosion source. To avoid vibration corrosion, the friction between the contact surfaces should be reduced (lubrication, shape, temperature, etc.), and can be avoided

There is stress concentration or stress concentration at the opening, under the action of stress F, the corrosion source is generated. Avoid stress corrosion by minimizing stress concentration on the surface, using liquid pressure, shock, etc., to increase the stress distribution in the chemical reaction of the corrosion medium and increase the corrosion resistance

sections.text: 2 Material Selection Under Corrosion Working Conditions
2.1 Atmospheric Corrosion

When the atmospheric relative humidity (RH) is greater than 75% or higher, the corrosion rate of metals in the atmosphere increases significantly. If the SO₂ concentration in the air reaches 0.01% or higher, the corrosion of metals will be significantly affected. According to the relative humidity of the atmosphere (RH), the atmospheric environment is divided into three types: dry type (RH<60%), normal type (75%>RH≥60%), humid type (RH≥75%). sections.text: 6 Elimination of Runout Error

Some machines require that there is no runout during operation. Runout errors are mainly caused by transmission device errors (such as gear runout, see Figure 5-5-13). Runout of the bearing machine affects operation difficulty. Reducing or eliminating spindle runout can be achieved by:

items: Reduce system-level transmission ratio and eliminate runout at the next level. See Figure 5-5-7, right gear 4 and its upper surface reserved for runout elimination.

In the transmission system, add a copper sleeve to make the system respond in time to one-sided tooth surface contact. See Figure 5-5-7, right gear 4 and its upper surface reserved for runout elimination.
Adjust the tooth center distance to reduce tooth side runout.
Support the bearing with floating elements and use strong pressure to reduce tooth side runout (Figure 5-5-14).

Use eccentric discs on the wheel to control runout. Place one (usually large diameter) on the gear shaft to form a sheet. sections.text: 3 Transmission Mechanism Error Transmission Accuracy Principle

In transmission systems, when the shaft speed changes due to transmission component errors or speed changes, the error difference changes with the speed change. Analyzing transmission component errors is important for understanding error transmission. If Figure 5-5-6 shows a speed reduction device with one pair of gears (the main shaft I and speed reduction shaft II have angular velocity errors) as Δ₁, and the other pair of gears has transmission motion errors Δ₂, Δ₃, Δ₄, then the total transmission system error (shaft V angular velocity error) is maximum at:
Δ = (Δ₁/(i₂i₃i₄) + Δ₂/(i₃i₄) + Δ₃/i₄ + Δ₄) + Δ₁

From the formula, if the final transmission ratio i₁ is relatively small (such as less than 200), the error Δ₁ of the last stage transmission has the least influence on the system error. For precision machinery, the final stage transmission should use a transmission ratio with large reduction ratio. This requires that the control precision of the transmission components be lower.

(2) Using thermal expansion to eliminate the error of rotating structure transmission

For precision transmission of rotating structures, worm gear transmission, screw transmission, and belt transmission devices, due to manufacturing errors and assembly errors, there will be transmission errors in the transmission system. If the transmission system has errors that can be measured, then the transmission system can add compensation mechanisms to reduce the error. 4 Error Averaging Principle—Adopting Multi-Point Contact to Improve Precision Standards

The error averaging principle is: in a machine, if there are multiple non-contact points that have a limiting effect on a certain motion, and the motion error is distributed among each contact point, the motion error of the machine is determined by the comprehensive effect of all contact points. For example, the screw pair in a screw transmission is used to limit the motion error by the comprehensive effect of multiple threads. Therefore, appropriately increasing the number of threads can improve the overall motion accuracy. This is the principle of error averaging.

The four shaft bearings use ball bearings, the shaft is positioned by support. These four shaft bearings use ball bearings, forming a self-aligning support point, ensuring error averaging and extending the service life of the spindle. 1 Design Principles Based on Human Morphology
1.1 Principles of Human Factors Engineering for Work System Design

The national standard GB/T 16251—2008 "Work System Design of Human Factors Engineering" stipulates the basic principles of work system design in human factors engineering (also called human-machine engineering). This standard specifies design principles applicable to optimizing the work environment design, focusing on human activity quantity, safety and health, and also emphasizes the technical and economic benefits of the results. This standard's principles are not only applicable to work system design, but also applicable to other designs related to human activities. This standard is a core standard for human factors effectiveness, and many other standards for specific issues are based on this standard.

5 Principles of Reasonable Error Allocation and Control

For machine tool equipment, the accuracy of related components must be reasonably allocated. If the accuracy is not properly allocated, it will affect the assembly accuracy and the overall accuracy of the machine tool. If the accuracy is too high, it will increase the processing cost and difficulty. If the accuracy is too low, it will reduce the accuracy of the machine tool. Figure 5-5-11 shows the main shaft bearing accuracy allocation and control method.

1) The bearing precision grade after the rear bearing is high. If Figure 5-5-11 has two bearings, one bearing precision grade (referring to the radial runout of the bearing) is low (referring to the axial runout of the bearing). If the high precision bearing is installed on the rear bearing (Figure 5-5-11a), the main spindle diameter error is:
δ₁ = (L+a)/L × δ
If the high precision bearing is installed on the front bearing (Figure 5-5-11b), the main spindle diameter error is:
δ₂ = a/L × δ
Since δ₁ > δ₂, the front bearing precision should be higher than the rear bearing.
2) The maximum radial runout of the two bearings is in the same direction. Figure 5-5-12 shows the maximum radial runout of the front and rear bearings as δₐ and δᵦ. See the figure below.

sections.text: 5 Design Principles Based on Human Sensory Organ Requirements

For mechanical design, the most important human sensory organs are vision, hearing, and touch. People recognize about 80% of information in the world through vision. When driving through traffic, starting various machine tools, using test instruments, etc., vision is always emphasized as having the most information. Therefore, the design of sensory organs must meet the observation requirements of users. Consider facilitating observation, having clear sensory organs, being observed by the human body without obstruction, having sufficient size, being able to quickly and accurately obtain information.

Hand-controlled manipulators are used for fine adjustment, quick adjustment, and can be used for coarse adjustment. When using fine adjustment and inspection, at the first one-time continuous rotation angle is 120° should be used. 2) The lever is used for rough, large-amplitude adjustment, and the fine adjustment should not be too large. 3) Manipulators are suitable for activities in confined spaces with limited visibility, and coarse adjustment is performed. 4) Key-press and rotary-rod types are suitable for push-button control lines with smooth on-off. 5) Rotary-rod type is used for two-way or multi-position adjustment. 6) Rotary-rod type is used for small-angle fine adjustment or multi-position adjustment.
Foot-controlled manipulators: such as pedals, pedal plates, pedal rods, etc.

Foot-controlled manipulators are used for automatic operation, quick adjustment, and are suitable for large-force operations. Foot-controlled manipulators are located in a safe position with good visibility.

sections.caption: Table 5-6-26 General Ergonomic Requirements for Manipulators
rows: 1) When using a finger-operated manipulator, the hand-contact part should be spherical, round-shaped, and should not have sharp edges or corners. The contact surface should have appropriate roughness, and the hand-contact part should have a suitable shape and size to ensure comfortable operation. The operation should be smooth and round-shaped (see Figure a). 2) To ensure visual observation of the indicator, the indicator should be clear and easy to read. The hand can control the round shape or round shape (see Figure a).

3) Dual-hand manipulators with hand-operated handles should be 120° apart, and the hand-operated handles should be combined to ensure that the hand-operated handles are not easily opened or closed. The hand-operated handles should be installed on the wheel to prevent the hand from sliding off the wheel. 4) Hand-operated manipulators should have a rotation angle of no more than 90°, and should not exceed 120° (see Figure b). 5) Manipulator lever angle should be 30°-60° from horizontal, and should not exceed 90°. 6) Hand-operated manipulators should have a smooth surface with appropriate shape, using hand-operated buttons with a surface area of 3-5 mm diameter, which can form a smooth plane shape. If it is a coded groove, it should be prevented from forming a flat shape (see Figure c).

7) Hand-operated manipulator lever opening angle should be single-hole shape, and the lever or lever position should be clearly marked. The lever structure should be clearly marked outside, and the lever structure should be clearly marked. 8) Hand-operated manipulator in the manipulator should be in a fixed position, and the hand-operated handle should be rotated to another position at the same time, and the hand-operated handle should be rotated to the side or side position, and should not be easily opened or closed. 9) Hand-operated manipulator surface temperature: 10°C or below 60°C. When using a guide system, the material should be selected according to the material. 10) Hand-operated manipulator should not be used for continuous operation in the hand-operated position. sections.text: 1.3 Principles for Avoiding Injury from Operating Errors

Figure 5-7-1 shows a machine tool. After the operator's hand enters the work area, before pressing the start button, if the operator's hand is not removed from the work area, another hand should move the chuck. If the hand is not removed at that time, another hand moving the chuck may cause hand injury. For this reason, the designer should design the chuck to move left and right, so that the work piece is clamped with both hands simultaneously pressing left and right chucks. The machine cannot start until both chucks are open, thus preventing hand injuries from occurring.

2.2 Design Principles for Noise Reduction

(1) Reduce noise at the source. The copper plate of the locomotive is the main source of noise. Every 1000m to the left and right, there is a noise source. The locomotive's wheels, rails, and other components generate noise. If the locomotive is equipped with sound insulation and vibration isolation devices, and combined with sound-absorbing materials (such as metal sound-absorbing plates), the noise can be reduced by 10dB(A). If changed to 10dB(A) sound-absorbing materials, the noise can be reduced by 93dB(A). This can be considered for use in areas where noise reduction is required. Using low-noise materials (such as rubber), the noise can be reduced to a lower level, but the impact of vibration changes must be considered.

Chapter 8 Green Design
1 Green Design and Common Key Technologies for Product Green Design

sections.caption: Table 5-8-1
rows: Green design is the design of products in the production and life cycle, fully considering the design of environmental impact reduction. The design requirements can be summarized into 3R1D, namely: (1) Reduce (Reduce) - reduce the amount of raw materials used in the product, reduce or eliminate pollution to the environment; (2) Reuse (Reuse) - products can be reused, recycled and reused; (3) Recycle (Recycle) - materials are easy to recycle and reuse; (4) Degrade (Degradable) - products can be degraded and decomposed, not polluting the environment

Product life cycle design includes raw material acquisition, processing, manufacturing, product formation, storage, transportation, sales, use, etc. The entire product life cycle should be considered. The life cycle design standard is that the product has a long service life, good performance, low cost, and can be recycled and reused in various ways to reduce environmental pollution

Disassembly is an important research topic in green design. The main points are: disassembly should be considered in the product design stage, the disassembly sequence should be clear, the number of disassembly steps should be small, the disassembly time should be short, and the material separation should be easy to reduce the complexity of materials

Resource recovery and reuse is the main goal of reverse design. We must first clarify the concept of 'product recycling', define it as 'using the product's entire life cycle and management guidelines, using materials, processes, structures, and environmental protection targets, modifying and improving the product structure and system technology to improve the product's recovery and reuse rate. In the third industry (including automotive, electrical appliances, tires, and packaging), it accounts for 70%, and in the fourth industry (including automobiles, electrical appliances, tires, and packaging), it accounts for 90% or more

(1) Analyze the reasons for product failure in various parts, improve the design, and extend the service life; (2) Use modular design, layered design, and design that can be upgraded, allowing products to be continuously upgraded without being eliminated by the market, reducing the rate of product elimination
Use the latest technology to make products consume less energy during use, reducing energy loss

Modular design is to divide the product into functional modules based on the basic modules, plan and design a series of functional modules, and combine them to form multiple products according to requirements. This type of product can perform modular maintenance, avoid the constraints of the lower module, and is not a mechanical assembly. If the module can be used to repair and replace the module, it can be further improved to achieve green design goals

sections.text: (4) Prevention of vibration and noise at the shared bearing support

sections.text: 4 Green Product Design for Energy Saving

The key to achieving green product design for energy saving is to implement energy-saving discharge as the main selection criterion. The entire lifecycle of product production—from material and energy consumption, material processing into machine parts, through processing, assembly, testing, packaging, transportation, installation, use, maintenance, to the end of product life—must be considered. For waste machine disposal, follow the principle of classification and recycling, and use scientific and rational methods. The entire process should have minimal waste discharge. It is necessary to follow the principle of "one examination, one assessment, one use of clean materials and human effort, and to find the best solution for energy saving and discharge." For example, in fans, pipelines, bearings and other components, report the discharge method afterwards to avoid improper handling.

items: Scrap: extract alloy composition, cast iron, copper materials, and other materials; classify and process, smelt out copper alloy, cast iron, steel materials and other materials.
Disassembly method: classify and process. Some parts can be directly reused, or processed and reused later. Other components can be recycled.

sections.text: Using these two methods, whichever method meets the requirements for energy-saving discharge must be determined through detailed comparison and calculation to determine which approach is more reasonable.
